projections.label: Activate temperature control
projections.tooltip:
Enable this option for automated chamber temperature control. This option activates the emitting of an M191 command before the "machine_start_gcode"
 which sets the chamber temperature and waits until it is reached. In addition, it emits an M141 command at the end of the print to turn off the chamber heater, if present.

This option relies on the firmware supporting the M191 and M141 commands either via macros or natively and is usually used when an active chamber heater is installed.

projections.label: Mesh margin

projections.label: Pressure advance for bridges
projections.tooltip:
Pressure advance value for bridges. Set to 0 to disable.

A lower PA value when printing bridges helps reduce the appearance of slight under extrusion immediately after bridges. This is caused by the pressure drop in the nozzle when printing in the air and a lower PA helps counteract this.

projections.label: Adaptive pressure advance measurements (beta)
projections.tooltip:
Add sets of pressure advance (PA) values, the volumetric flow speeds and accelerations they were measured at, separated by a comma. One set of values per line. For example
0.04,3.96,3000
0.033,3.96,10000
0.029,7.91,3000
0.026,7.91,10000

How to calibrate:
1. Run the pressure advance test for at least 3 speeds per acceleration value. It is recommended that the test is run for at least the speed of the external perimeters, the speed of the internal perimeters and the fastest feature print speed in your profile (usually its the sparse or solid infill). Then run them for the same speeds for the slowest and fastest print accelerations, and no faster than the recommended maximum acceleration as given by the Klipper input shaper
2. Take note of the optimal PA value for each volumetric flow speed and acceleration. You can find the flow number by selecting flow from the color scheme drop down and move the horizontal slider over the PA pattern lines. The number should be visible at the bottom of the page. The ideal PA value should be decreasing the higher the volumetric flow is. If it is not, confirm that your extruder is functioning correctly. The slower and with less acceleration you print, the larger the range of acceptable PA values. If no difference is visible, use the PA value from the faster test
3. Enter the triplets of PA values, Flow and Accelerations in the text box here and save your filament profile

projections.label: Enable adaptive pressure advance for overhangs (beta)
projections.tooltip: Enable adaptive PA for overhangs as well as when flow changes within the same feature. This is an experimental option, as if the PA profile is not set accurately, it will cause uniformity issues on the external surfaces before and after overhangs.

projections.label: Enable adaptive pressure advance (beta)
projections.tooltip:
With increasing print speeds (and hence increasing volumetric flow through the nozzle) and increasing accelerations, it has been observed that the effective PA value typically decreases. This means that a single PA value is not always 100% optimal for all features and a compromise value is usually used that does not cause too much bulging on features with lower flow speed and accelerations while also not causing gaps on faster features.

This feature aims to address this limitation by modeling the response of your printer's extrusion system depending on the volumetric flow speed and acceleration it is printing at. Internally, it generates a fitted model that can extrapolate the needed pressure advance for any given volumetric flow speed and acceleration, which is then emitted to the printer depending on the current print conditions.

When enabled, the pressure advance value above is overridden. However, a reasonable default value above is strongly recommended to act as a fallback and for when tool changing.

projections.label: Fan speed
projections.tooltip:
Speed of auxiliary part cooling fan. Auxiliary fan will run at this speed during printing except the first several layers which is defined by no cooling layers.
Please enable auxiliary_fan in printer settings to use this feature. G-code command: M106 P2 S(0-255)

projections.label: Align infill direction to model
projections.tooltip: Aligns infill and surface fill directions to follow the model's orientation on the build plate. When enabled, fill directions rotate with the model to maintain optimal strength characteristics.

projections.label: Alternate extra wall
projections.tooltip:
This setting adds an extra wall to every other layer. This way the infill gets wedged vertically between the walls, resulting in stronger prints.

When this option is enabled, the ensure vertical shell thickness option needs to be disabled.

Using lightning infill together with this option is not recommended as there is limited infill to anchor the extra perimeters to.

projections.label: Auxiliary part cooling fan
projections.tooltip: Enable this option if machine has auxiliary part cooling fan. G-code command: M106 P2 S(0-255).

projections.label: Bed mesh max
projections.tooltip: This option sets the max point for the allowed bed mesh area. Due to the probe's XY offset, most printers are unable to probe the entire bed. To ensure the probe point does not go outside the bed area, the minimum and maximum points of the bed mesh should be set appropriately. Snapmaker_Orca ensures that adaptive_bed_mesh_min/adaptive_bed_mesh_max values do not exceed these min/max points. This information can usually be obtained from your printer manufacturer. The default setting is (99999, 99999), which means there are no limits, thus allowing probing across the entire bed.

projections.label: Bed mesh min
projections.tooltip: This option sets the min point for the allowed bed mesh area. Due to the probe's XY offset, most printers are unable to probe the entire bed. To ensure the probe point does not go outside the bed area, the minimum and maximum points of the bed mesh should be set appropriately. Snapmaker Orca ensures that adaptive_bed_mesh_min/adaptive_bed_mesh_max values do not exceed these min/max points. This information can usually be obtained from your printer manufacturer. The default setting is (-99999, -99999), which means there are no limits, thus allowing probing across the entire bed.

projections.label: Probe point distance
projections.tooltip: This option sets the preferred distance between probe points (grid size) for the X and Y directions, with the default being 50mm for both X and Y.

projections.label: Before layer change G-code
projections.tooltip: This G-code is inserted at every layer change before the Z lift.

projections.label: Best object position
projections.tooltip: Best auto arranging position in range [0,1] w.r.t. bed shape.

projections.label: Bottom shell layers
projections.tooltip: This is the number of solid layers of bottom shell, including the bottom surface layer. When the thickness calculated by this value is thinner than bottom shell thickness, the bottom shell layers will be increased.

projections.label: Bottom shell thickness
projections.tooltip: The number of bottom solid layers is increased when slicing if the thickness calculated by bottom shell layers is thinner than this value. This can avoid having too thin shell when layer height is small. 0 means that this setting is disabled and thickness of bottom shell is absolutely determined by bottom shell layers.

projections.label: Bottom surface flow ratio
projections.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for bottom solid infill.

The actual bottom solid infill flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

projections.label: Bottom surface density
projections.tooltip:
Density of the bottom surface layer. Intended for aesthetic or functional purposes, not to fix issues such as over-extrusion.
WARNING: Lowering this value may negatively affect bed adhesion.

projections.label: Bottom surface pattern
projections.tooltip: Line pattern of bottom surface infill, not bridge infill.

projections.label: Bridge
projections.tooltip: Acceleration of bridges. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 50%), it will be calculated based on the outer wall acceleration.

projections.label: External bridge infill direction
projections.tooltip: Bridging angle override. If left to zero, the bridging angle will be calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided angle will be used for external bridges. Use 180°for zero angle.

projections.label: External bridge density
projections.tooltip:
Controls the density (spacing) of external bridge lines. 100% means solid bridge. Default is 100%.

Lower density external bridges can help improve reliability as there is more space for air to circulate around the extruded bridge, improving its cooling speed.

projections.label: Bridge flow ratio
projections.tooltip:
Decrease this value slightly (for example 0.9) to reduce the amount of material for bridge, to improve sag.

The actual bridge flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

projections.label: Don't support bridges
projections.tooltip: Don't support the whole bridge area which make support very large. Bridges can usually be printed directly without support if not very long.

projections.label: External
projections.tooltip:
Speed of the externally visible bridge extrusions.

In addition, if Slow down for curled perimeters is disabled or Classic overhang mode is enabled, it will be the print speed of overhang walls that are supported by less than 13%, whether they are part of a bridge or an overhang.

projections.label: Brim ear detection radius
projections.tooltip:
The geometry will be decimated before detecting sharp angles. This parameter indicates the minimum length of the deviation for the decimation.
0 to deactivate.

projections.label: Brim ear max angle
projections.tooltip:
Maximum angle to let a brim ear appear.
If set to 0, no brim will be created.
If set to ~180, brim will be created on everything but straight sections.

projections.label: Brim ears
projections.tooltip: Only draw brim over the sharp edges of the model.

projections.label: Brim-object gap
projections.tooltip: A gap between innermost brim line and object can make brim be removed more easily.

projections.label: Brim type
projections.tooltip: This controls the generation of the brim at outer and/or inner side of models. Auto means the brim width is analyzed and calculated automatically.

projections.label: Brim width
projections.tooltip: Distance from model to the outermost brim line.

projections.label: Chamber temperature
projections.tooltip:
For high-temperature materials like ABS, ASA, PC, and PA, a higher chamber temperature can help suppress or reduce warping and potentially lead to higher interlayer bonding strength. However, at the same time, a higher chamber temperature will reduce the efficiency of air filtration for ABS and ASA.

For PLA, PETG, TPU, PVA, and other low-temperature materials, this option should be disabled (set to 0) as the chamber temperature should be low to avoid extruder clogging caused by material softening at the heat break.

If enabled, this parameter also sets a G-code variable named chamber_temperature, which can be used to pass the desired chamber temperature to your print start macro, or a heat soak macro like this: PRINT_START (other variables) CHAMBER_TEMP=[chamber_temperature]. This may be useful if your printer does not support M141/M191 commands, or if you desire to handle heat soaking in the print start macro if no active chamber heater is installed.

projections.tooltip: A boolean expression using the configuration values of an active print profile. If this expression evaluates to true, this profile is considered compatible with the active print profile.

projections.label: Fan speed
projections.tooltip: Speed of exhaust fan after printing completes.

projections.label: Initial layer
projections.tooltip: Bed temperature of the initial layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Cool Plate.

projections.label: Other layers
projections.tooltip: Bed temperature for layers except the initial one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Cool Plate.

projections.label: Cooling tube length
projections.tooltip: Length of the cooling tube to limit space for cooling moves inside it.

projections.label: Cooling tube position
projections.tooltip: Distance of the center-point of the cooling tube from the extruder tip.

projections.label: Bridge counterbore holes
projections.tooltip:
This option creates bridges for counterbore holes, allowing them to be printed without support. Available modes include:
1. None: No bridge is created
2. Partially Bridged: Only a part of the unsupported area will be bridged
3. Sacrificial Layer: A full sacrificial bridge layer is created

projections.label: De-retraction Speed
projections.tooltip: Speed for reloading filament into the nozzle. Zero means same speed of retraction.

projections.label: Detect narrow internal solid infill
projections.tooltip: This option will auto-detect narrow internal solid infill areas. If enabled, the concentric pattern will be used for the area to speed up printing. Otherwise, the rectilinear pattern will be used by default.

projections.label: Detect overhang wall
projections.tooltip: Detect the overhang percentage relative to line width and use different speed to print. For 100%% overhang, bridge speed is used.

projections.label: Detect thin wall
projections.tooltip: Detect thin wall which can't contain two line width. And use single line to print. Maybe printed not very well, because it's not closed loop.

projections.label: Disable set remaining print time
projections.tooltip: Disable generating of the M73: Set remaining print time in the final G-code.

projections.label: Use direct multicolor Local-Z solver
projections.tooltip:
Experimental. For mixed rows with 3 or more physical filaments, allocate Local-Z sublayers directly across all components with carry-over error between layers instead of collapsing them into pair cadence.

This can reduce visible banding in multicolor Local-Z blends at the cost of more toolchanges. It is ignored when explicit Local-Z A/B heights are set.

projections.label: Apply subdivision to infill
projections.tooltip:
Experimental. When Subdivide Mix Layer is enabled, also apply the same subdivision to infill inside mixed-color areas.

This is enabled automatically with Subdivide Mix Layer. Turn it off to keep infill on the normal layer height.

It can improve internal color mixing, but may add toolchanges and affect infill behavior.

projections.label: Subdivide Mix Layer
projections.tooltip: Enable "Subdivide Mix Layer" for mixing areas. Layer height will be subdivided for better color mixing results.

projections.label: Full domain
projections.tooltip:
Experimental. Apply Local-Z thinning across whole mixed-color regions instead of limiting the effect strictly to painted mixed masks.

Only available when Subdivide Mix Layer is enabled.

projections.label: Use step size in painted zones only
projections.tooltip:
When enabled, dithering Z step size is applied only where mixed filament is painted. Unpainted zones keep their original layer height.

Detailed mixed filament setting explanations will be published once the project wiki is available.

projections.label: Dithering Z step size
projections.tooltip:
Layer height used in Z zones painted with dithering (mixed virtual filaments). Set to 0 to keep normal layer height in those zones.

Detailed mixed filament setting explanations will be published once the project wiki is available.

projections.label: Filter out small internal bridges
projections.tooltip:
This option can help reduce pillowing on top surfaces in heavily slanted or curved models.
By default, small internal bridges are filtered out and the internal solid infill is printed directly over the sparse infill. This works well in most cases, speeding up printing without too much compromise on top surface quality.
However, in heavily slanted or curved models, especially where too low a sparse infill density is used, this may result in curling of the unsupported solid infill, causing pillowing.
Enabling limited filtering or no filtering will print internal bridge layer over slightly unsupported internal solid infill. The options below control the sensitivity of the filtering, i.e. they control where internal bridges are created:
1. Filter - enables this option. This is the default behavior and works well in most cases
2. Limited filtering - creates internal bridges on heavily slanted surfaces while avoiding unnecessary bridges. This works well for most difficult models
3. No filtering - creates internal bridges on every potential internal overhang. This option is useful for heavily slanted top surface models; however, in most cases, it creates too many unnecessary bridges

projections.label: Don't slow down outer walls
projections.tooltip:
If enabled, this setting will ensure external perimeters are not slowed down to meet the minimum layer time. This is particularly helpful in the below scenarios:
1. To avoid changes in shine when printing glossy filaments
2. To avoid changes in external wall speed which may create slight wall artifacts that appear like Z banding
3. To avoid printing at speeds which cause VFAs (fine artifacts) on the external walls

projections.label: Draft shield
projections.tooltip:
A draft shield is useful to protect an ABS or ASA print from warping and detaching from print bed due to wind draft. It is usually needed only with open frame printers, i.e. without an enclosure.

Enabled = skirt is as tall as the highest printed object. Otherwise 'Skirt height' is used.
Note: With the draft shield active, the skirt will be printed at skirt distance from the object. Therefore, if brims are active it may intersect with them. To avoid this, increase the skirt distance value.

projections.label: Fan speed
projections.tooltip: Speed of exhaust fan during printing. This speed will override the speed in filament custom G-code.

projections.label: Emit limits to G-code
projections.tooltip:
If enabled, the machine limits will be emitted to G-code file.
This option will be ignored if the G-code flavor is set to Klipper.

projections.label: Arc fitting
projections.tooltip:
Enable this to get a G-code file which has G2 and G3 moves. The fitting tolerance is same as the resolution.

Note: For Klipper machines, this option is recommended to be disabled. Klipper does not benefit from arc commands as these are split again into line segments by the firmware. This results in a reduction in surface quality as line segments are converted to arcs by the slicer and then back to line segments by the firmware.

projections.label: Enable change pressure advance when wiping
projections.tooltip: If it's set to false, the pressure advance value will not be changed.

projections.label: Extra bridge layers (beta)
projections.tooltip:
This option enables the generation of an extra bridge layer over internal and/or external bridges.

Extra bridge layers help improve bridge appearance and reliability, as the solid infill is better supported. This is especially useful in fast printers, where the bridge and solid infill speeds vary greatly. The extra bridge layer results in reduced pillowing on top surfaces, as well as reduced separation of the external bridge layer from its surrounding perimeters.

It is generally recommended to set this to at least 'External bridge only', unless specific issues with the sliced model are found.

Options:
1. Disabled - does not generate second bridge layers. This is the default and is set for compatibility purposes
2. External bridge only - generates second bridge layers for external-facing bridges only. Please note that small bridges that are shorter or narrower than the set number of perimeters will be skipped as they would not benefit from a second bridge layer. If generated, the second bridge layer will be extruded parallel to the first bridge layer to reinforce the bridge strength
3. Internal bridge only - generates second bridge layers for internal bridges over sparse infill only. Please note that the internal bridges count towards the top shell layer count of your model. The second internal bridge layer will be extruded as close to perpendicular to the first as possible. If multiple regions in the same island, with varying bridge angles are present, the last region of that island will be selected as the angle reference
4. Apply to all - generates second bridge layers for both internal and external-facing bridges

projections.label: Enable filament ramming
projections.tooltip: Enable filament ramming

projections.label: Force cooling for overhangs and bridges
projections.tooltip: Enable this option to allow adjustment of the part cooling fan speed for specifically for overhangs, internal and external bridges. Setting the fan speed specifically for these features can improve overall print quality and reduce warping.

projections.label: Slow down for overhang
projections.tooltip: Enable this option to slow printing down for different overhang degree.

projections.label: Enable pressure advance
projections.tooltip: Enable pressure advance, auto calibration result will be overwritten once enabled.

projections.label: Enable
projections.tooltip: The wiping tower can be used to clean up the residue on the nozzle and stabilize the chamber pressure inside the nozzle, in order to avoid appearance defects when printing objects.

projections.label: Enable support
projections.tooltip: Enable support generation.

projections.label: Initial layer
projections.tooltip: Bed temperature of the initial layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Engineering Plate.

projections.label: Other layers
projections.tooltip: Bed temperature for layers except the initial one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Engineering Plate.

projections.label: Ensure vertical shell thickness
projections.tooltip:
Add solid infill near sloping surfaces to guarantee the vertical shell thickness (top+bottom solid layers)
None: No solid infill will be added anywhere. Caution: Use this option carefully if your model has sloped surfaces
Critical Only: Avoid adding solid infill for walls
Moderate: Add solid infill for heavily sloping surfaces only
All: Add solid infill for all suitable sloping surfaces
Default value is All.

projections.label: Exclude objects
projections.tooltip: Enable this option to add EXCLUDE OBJECT command in G-code.

projections.label: Extra loading distance
projections.tooltip: When set to zero, the distance the filament is moved from parking position during load is exactly the same as it was moved back during unload. When positive, it is loaded further, if negative, the loading move is shorter than unloading.

projections.label: Extra perimeters on overhangs
projections.tooltip: Create additional perimeter paths over steep overhangs and areas where bridges cannot be anchored.

projections.label: Insert solid layers
projections.tooltip: Insert solid infill at specific layers. Use N to insert every Nth layer, N#K to insert K consecutive solid layers every N layers (K is optional, e.g. '5#' equals '5#1'), or a comma-separated list (e.g. 1,7,9) to insert at explicit layers. Layers are 1-based.

projections.label: Height to lid
projections.tooltip: Distance of the nozzle tip to the lid. Used for collision avoidance in by-object printing.

projections.label: Height to rod
projections.tooltip: Distance of the nozzle tip to the lower rod. Used for collision avoidance in by-object printing.

projections.label: Radius
projections.tooltip: Clearance radius around extruder. Used for collision avoidance in by-object printing.

projections.label: Extruder Color
projections.tooltip: Only used as a visual help on UI.

projections.label: Apply only on external features
projections.tooltip: Applies extrusion rate smoothing only on external perimeters and overhangs. This can help reduce artefacts due to sharp speed transitions on externally visible overhangs without impacting the print speed of features that will not be visible to the user.

projections.label: Layer time
projections.tooltip: Part cooling fan will be enabled for layers of which estimated time is shorter than this value. Fan speed is interpolated between the minimum and maximum fan speeds according to layer printing time.

projections.label: Fan kick-start time
projections.tooltip:
Emit a max fan speed command for this amount of seconds before reducing to target speed to kick-start the cooling fan.
This is useful for fans where a low PWM/power may be insufficient to get the fan started spinning from a stop, or to get the fan up to speed faster.
Set to 0 to deactivate.

projections.label: Fan speed
projections.tooltip: Part cooling fan speed may be increased when auto cooling is enabled. This is the maximum speed for the part cooling fan.

projections.label: Fan speed
projections.tooltip: Minimum speed for part cooling fan.

projections.label: Only overhangs
projections.tooltip: Will only take into account the delay for the cooling of overhangs.

projections.label: fan_speedup_time
projections.tooltip:
Start the fan this number of seconds earlier than its target start time (you can use fractional seconds). It assumes infinite acceleration for this time estimation, and will only take into account G1 and G0 moves (arc fitting is unsupported).
It won't move fan commands from custom G-code (they act as a sort of 'barrier').
It won't move fan commands into the start G-code if the 'only custom start G-code' is activated.
Use 0 to deactivate.

projections.label: Color
projections.tooltip: Only used as a visual help on UI.

projections.label: Speed of the last cooling move
projections.tooltip: Cooling moves are gradually accelerating towards this speed.

projections.label: Speed of the first cooling move
projections.tooltip: Cooling moves are gradually accelerating beginning at this speed.

projections.label: Number of cooling moves
projections.tooltip: Filament is cooled by being moved back and forth in the cooling tubes. Specify desired number of these moves.

projections.label: Price
projections.tooltip: Filament price. For statistics only.

projections.label: Density
projections.tooltip: Filament density. For statistics only.

projections.label: De-retraction Speed
projections.tooltip: Speed for reloading filament into the nozzle. Zero means same speed of retraction.

projections.label: Diameter
projections.tooltip: Filament diameter is used to calculate extrusion in G-code, so it is important and should be accurate.

projections.label: End G-code
projections.tooltip: End G-code when finishing the printing of this filament.

projections.label: Flow ratio
projections.tooltip: The material may have volumetric change after switching between molten and crystalline states. This setting changes all extrusion flow of this filament in G-code proportionally. The recommended value range is between 0.95 and 1.05. You may be able to tune this value to get a nice flat surface if there is slight overflow or underflow.

projections.label: Support material
projections.tooltip: Support material is commonly used to print supports and support interfaces.

projections.label: Loading speed at the start
projections.tooltip: Speed used at the very beginning of loading phase.

projections.label: Loading speed
projections.tooltip: Speed used for loading the filament on the wipe tower.

projections.label: Long retraction when cut (beta)
projections.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retracting and cutting off the filament at a longer distance during changes to minimize purge. While this reduces flush significantly, it may also raise the risk of nozzle clogs or other printing problems.

projections.label: Max volumetric speed
projections.tooltip: This setting stands for how much volume of filament can be melted and extruded per second. Printing speed is limited by max volumetric speed, in case of too high and unreasonable speed setting. Can't be zero.

projections.label: Minimal purge on wipe tower
projections.tooltip: After a tool change, the exact position of the newly loaded filament inside the nozzle may not be known, and the filament pressure is likely not yet stable. Before purging the print head into an infill or a sacrificial object, Snapmaker Orca will always prime this amount of material into the wipe tower to produce successive infill or sacrificial object extrusions reliably.

projections.label: Multi-tool ramming flow
projections.tooltip: Flow used for ramming the filament before the tool change.

projections.label: Multi-tool ramming volume
projections.tooltip: The volume to be rammed before the tool change.

projections.label: Enable ramming for multi-tool setups
projections.tooltip: Perform ramming when using multi-tool printer (i.e. when the 'Single Extruder Multimaterial' in Printer Settings is unchecked). When checked, a small amount of filament is rapidly extruded on the wipe tower just before the tool change. This option is only used when the wipe tower is enabled.

projections.label: Filament notes
projections.tooltip: You can put your notes regarding the filament here.

projections.label: Ramming parameters
projections.tooltip: This string is edited by RammingDialog and contains ramming specific parameters.

projections.label: Retract amount before wipe
projections.tooltip: The length of fast retraction before wipe, relative to retraction length.

projections.label: Only lift Z above
projections.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place above the specified absolute Z.

projections.label: Only lift Z below
projections.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place below the specified absolute Z.

projections.label: On surfaces
projections.tooltip: Enforce Z-Hop behavior. This setting is impacted by the above settings (Only lift Z above/below).

projections.label: Extra length on restart
projections.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after changing tool, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament.

projections.label: Extra length on restart
projections.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after the travel move, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament. This setting is rarely needed.

projections.label: Retract when change layer
projections.tooltip: Force a retraction when changes layer.

projections.label: Retraction distance when cut
projections.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retraction length before cutting off during filament change.

projections.label: Length
projections.tooltip: Some amount of material in extruder is pulled back to avoid ooze during long travel. Set zero to disable retraction.

projections.label: Travel distance threshold
projections.tooltip: Only trigger retraction when the travel distance is longer than this threshold.

projections.label: Retraction Speed
projections.tooltip: Speed for retracting filament from the nozzle.

projections.label: Shrinkage (XY)
projections.tooltip:
Enter the shrinkage percentage that the filament will get after cooling (94% if you measure 94mm instead of 100mm). The part will be scaled in xy to compensate. Only the filament used for the perimeter is taken into account.
Be sure to allow enough space between objects, as this compensation is done after the checks.

projections.label: Shrinkage (Z)
projections.tooltip: Enter the shrinkage percentage that the filament will get after cooling (94% if you measure 94mm instead of 100mm). The part will be scaled in Z to compensate.

projections.label: Soluble material
projections.tooltip: Soluble material is commonly used to print supports and support interfaces.

projections.label: Stamping distance measured from the center of the cooling tube
projections.tooltip: If set to non-zero value, filament is moved toward the nozzle between the individual cooling moves ("stamping"). This option configures how long this movement should be before the filament is retracted again.

projections.label: Stamping loading speed
projections.tooltip: Speed used for stamping.

projections.label: Start G-code
projections.tooltip: Start G-code when starting the printing of this filament.

projections.label: Delay after unloading
projections.tooltip: Time to wait after the filament is unloaded. May help to get reliable tool changes with flexible materials that may need more time to shrink to original dimensions.

projections.label: Type
projections.tooltip: The material type of filament.

projections.label: Unloading speed at the start
projections.tooltip: Speed used for unloading the tip of the filament immediately after ramming.

projections.label: Unloading speed
projections.tooltip: Speed used for unloading the filament on the wipe tower (does not affect initial part of unloading just after ramming).

projections.label: Vendor
projections.tooltip: Vendor of filament. For show only.

projections.label: Wipe Distance
projections.tooltip:
Describe how long the nozzle will move along the last path when retracting.

Depending on how long the wipe operation lasts, how fast and long the extruder/filament retraction settings are, a retraction move may be needed to retract the remaining filament.

Setting a value in the retract amount before wipe setting below will perform any excess retraction before the wipe, else it will be performed after.

projections.label: Wipe while retracting
projections.tooltip: Move nozzle along the last extrusion path when retracting to clean any leaked material on the nozzle. This can minimize blobs when printing a new part after traveling.

projections.label: Z-hop type
projections.tooltip: Type of Z-hop.

projections.label: Z-hop height
projections.tooltip: Whenever the retraction is done, the nozzle is lifted a little to create clearance between nozzle and the print. It prevents nozzle from hitting the print when travel move. Using spiral lines to lift Z can prevent stringing.

projections.label: Filename format
projections.tooltip: Users can define the project file name when exporting.

projections.label: Fill Multiline
projections.tooltip: Using multiple lines for the infill pattern, if supported by infill pattern.

projections.label: Filter out tiny gaps
projections.tooltip: Don't print gap fill with a length is smaller than the threshold specified (in mm). This setting applies to top, bottom and solid infill and, if using the classic perimeter generator, to wall gap fill.

projections.label: Flush into objects' infill
projections.tooltip: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' infills. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. If the walls are printed with transparent filament, the mixed color infill will be seen outside. It will not take effect, unless the prime tower is enabled.

projections.label: Flush into this object
projections.tooltip: This object will be used to purge the nozzle after a filament change to save filament and decrease the print time. Colors of the objects will be mixed as a result. It will not take effect unless the prime tower is enabled.

projections.label: Flush into objects' support
projections.tooltip: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' support. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. It will not take effect, unless the prime tower is enabled.

projections.label: Flush multiplier
projections.tooltip: The actual flushing volumes is equal to the flush multiplier multiplied by the flushing volumes in the table.

projections.label: Full fan speed at layer
projections.tooltip: Fan speed will be ramped up linearly from zero at layer "close_fan_the_first_x_layers" to maximum at layer "full_fan_speed_layer". "full_fan_speed_layer" will be ignored if lower than "close_fan_the_first_x_layers", in which case the fan will be running at maximum allowed speed at layer "close_fan_the_first_x_layers" + 1.

projections.label: Apply fuzzy skin to first layer
projections.tooltip: Whether to apply fuzzy skin on the first layer.

projections.label: Fuzzy skin generator mode
projections.tooltip:
Fuzzy skin generation mode. Works only with Arachne!
Displacement: Сlassic mode when the pattern is formed by shifting the nozzle sideways from the original path.
Extrusion: The mode when the pattern formed by the amount of extruded plastic. This is the fast and straight algorithm without unnecessary nozzle shake that gives a smooth pattern. But it is more useful for forming loose walls in the entire they array.
Combined: Joint mode [Displacement] + [Extrusion]. The appearance of the walls is similar to [Displacement] Mode, but it leaves no pores between the perimeters.

Attention! The [Extrusion] and [Combined] modes works only the fuzzy_skin_thickness parameter not more than the thickness of printed loop. At the same time, the width of the extrusion for a particular layer should also not be below a certain level. It is usually equal 15-25%% of a layer height. Therefore, the maximum fuzzy skin thickness with a perimeter width of 0.4 mm and a layer height of 0.2 mm will be 0.4-(0.2*0.25)=±0.35mm! If you enter a higher parameter than this, the error Flow::spacing() will displayed, and the model will not be sliced. You can choose this number until this error is repeated.

projections.label: Fuzzy skin noise type
projections.tooltip:
Noise type to use for fuzzy skin generation:
Classic: Classic uniform random noise.
Perlin: Perlin noise, which gives a more consistent texture.
Billow: Similar to perlin noise, but clumpier.
Ridged Multifractal: Ridged noise with sharp, jagged features. Creates marble-like textures.
Voronoi: Divides the surface into voronoi cells, and displaces each one by a random amount. Creates a patchwork texture.

projections.label: Fuzzy Skin Noise Octaves
projections.tooltip: The number of octaves of coherent noise to use. Higher values increase the detail of the noise, but also increase computation time.

projections.label: Fuzzy skin noise persistence
projections.tooltip: The decay rate for higher octaves of the coherent noise. Lower values will result in smoother noise.

projections.label: Fuzzy skin point distance
projections.tooltip: The average distance between the random points introduced on each line segment.

projections.label: Fuzzy skin feature size
projections.tooltip: The base size of the coherent noise features, in mm. Higher values will result in larger features.

projections.label: Fuzzy skin thickness
projections.tooltip: The width within which to jitter. It's advised to be below outer wall line width.

projections.label: Fuzzy Skin
projections.tooltip: Randomly jitter while printing the wall, so that the surface has a rough look. This setting controls the fuzzy position.

projections.label: Apply gap fill
projections.tooltip:
Enables gap fill for the selected solid surfaces. The minimum gap length that will be filled can be controlled from the filter out tiny gaps option below.

Options:
1. Everywhere: Applies gap fill to top, bottom and internal solid surfaces for maximum strength
2. Top and Bottom surfaces: Applies gap fill to top and bottom surfaces only, balancing print speed, reducing potential over extrusion in the solid infill and making sure the top and bottom surfaces have no pinhole gaps
3. Nowhere: Disables gap fill for all solid infill areas

Note that if using the classic perimeter generator, gap fill may also be generated between perimeters, if a full width line cannot fit between them. That perimeter gap fill is not controlled by this setting.

If you would like all gap fill, including the classic perimeter generated one, removed, set the filter out tiny gaps value to a large number, like 999999.

However this is not advised, as gap fill between perimeters is contributing to the model's strength. For models where excessive gap fill is generated between perimeters, a better option would be to switch to the arachne wall generator and use this option to control whether the cosmetic top and bottom surface gap fill is generated.

projections.label: Gap infill
projections.tooltip: Speed of gap infill. Gap usually has irregular line width and should be printed more slowly.

projections.label: Add line number
projections.tooltip: Enable this to add line number(Nx) at the beginning of each G-code line.

projections.label: Verbose G-code
projections.tooltip: Enable this to get a commented G-code file, with each line explained by a descriptive text. If you print from SD card, the additional weight of the file could make your firmware slow down.

projections.label: G-code flavor
projections.tooltip: What kind of G-code the printer is compatible with.

projections.label: Label objects
projections.tooltip: Enable this to add comments into the G-code labeling print moves with what object they belong to, which is useful for the Octoprint CancelObject plugin. This settings is NOT compatible with Single Extruder Multi Material setup and Wipe into Object / Wipe into Infill.

projections.label: Initial layer
projections.tooltip: Bed temperature of the initial layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Graphic Effect Plate.

projections.label: Other layers
projections.tooltip: Bed temperature for layers except the initial one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Graphic Effect Plate.

projections.label: High extruder current on filament swap
projections.tooltip: It may be beneficial to increase the extruder motor current during the filament exchange sequence to allow for rapid ramming feed rates and to overcome resistance when loading a filament with an ugly shaped tip.

projections.label: Polyhole detection margin
projections.tooltip:
Maximum defection of a point to the estimated radius of the circle.
As cylinders are often exported as triangles of varying size, points may not be on the circle circumference. This setting allows you some leeway to broaden the detection.
In mm or in % of the radius.

projections.label: Polyhole twist
projections.tooltip: Rotate the polyhole every layer.

projections.label: Convert holes to polyholes
projections.tooltip:
Search for almost-circular holes that span more than one layer and convert the geometry to polyholes. Use the nozzle size and the (biggest) diameter to compute the polyhole.
See http://hydraraptor.blogspot.com/2011/02/polyholes.html

projections.label: Host Type
projections.tooltip: Snapmaker Orca can upload G-code files to a printer host. This field must contain the kind of the host.

projections.label: Initial layer
projections.tooltip: Bed temperature of the initial layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the High Temp Plate.

projections.label: Other layers
projections.tooltip: Bed temperature for layers except the initial one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the High Temp Plate.

projections.label: Idle temperature
projections.tooltip: Nozzle temperature when the tool is currently not used in multi-tool setups. This is only used when 'Ooze prevention' is active in Print Settings. Set to 0 to disable.

projections.label: Independent support layer height
projections.tooltip: Support layer uses layer height independent with object layer. This is to support customizing z-gap and save print time. This option will be invalid when the prime tower is enabled.

projections.label: Maximum length of the infill anchor
projections.tooltip:
Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. Snapmaker Orca tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than this parameter is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to infill_anchor, but no longer than this parameter.
If set to 0, the old algorithm for infill connection will be used, it should create the same result as with 1000 & 0.

projections.label: Sparse infill anchor length
projections.tooltip:
Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. Snapmaker Orca tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than infill_anchor_max is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to this parameter, but no longer than anchor_length_max.
Set this parameter to zero to disable anchoring perimeters connected to a single infill line.

projections.label: Infill combination - Max layer height
projections.tooltip:
Maximum layer height for the combined sparse infill.

Set it to 0 or 100% to use the nozzle diameter (for maximum reduction in print time) or a value of ~80% to maximize sparse infill strength.

The number of layers over which infill is combined is derived by dividing this value with the layer height and rounded down to the nearest decimal.

Use either absolute mm values (eg. 0.32mm for a 0.4mm nozzle) or % values (eg 80%). This value must not be larger than the nozzle diameter.

projections.label: Infill combination
projections.tooltip: Automatically Combine sparse infill of several layers to print together to reduce time. Wall is still printed with original layer height.

projections.label: Sparse infill direction
projections.tooltip: Angle for sparse infill pattern, which controls the start or main direction of line.

projections.label: Infill
projections.tooltip: Jerk for infill.

projections.label: Infill lock depth
projections.tooltip: The parameter sets the overlapping depth between the interior and skin.

projections.label: Infill overhang angle
projections.tooltip: The angle of the infill angled lines. 60° will result in a pure honeycomb.

projections.label: Infill shift step
projections.tooltip: This parameter adds a slight displacement to each layer of infill to create a cross texture.

projections.label: Infill/Wall overlap
projections.tooltip: Infill area is enlarged slightly to overlap with wall for better bonding. The percentage value is relative to line width of sparse infill. Set this value to ~10-15% to minimize potential over extrusion and accumulation of material resulting in rough top surfaces.

projections.label: Inherits profile
projections.tooltip: Name of parent profile.

projections.label: Initial layer
projections.tooltip: Acceleration of initial layer. Using a lower value can improve build plate adhesion.

projections.label: Initial layer infill
projections.tooltip: Speed of solid infill part of initial layer.

projections.label: Initial layer
projections.tooltip: Jerk for initial layer.

projections.label: Initial layer
projections.tooltip: Line width of initial layer. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

projections.label: First layer minimum wall width
projections.tooltip: The minimum wall width that should be used for the first layer is recommended to be set to the same size as the nozzle. This adjustment is expected to enhance adhesion.

projections.label: Initial layer height
projections.tooltip: Height of initial layer. Making initial layer height to be thick slightly can improve build plate adhesion.

projections.label: Initial layer
projections.tooltip: Speed of initial layer except the solid infill part.

projections.label: Initial layer travel speed
projections.tooltip: Travel speed of initial layer.

projections.label: Inner wall
projections.tooltip: Acceleration of inner walls.

projections.label: Inner wall
projections.tooltip: Jerk of inner walls.

projections.label: Inner wall
projections.tooltip: Line width of inner wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

projections.label: Inner wall
projections.tooltip: Speed of inner wall.

projections.label: Interface shells
projections.tooltip: Force the generation of solid shells between adjacent materials/volumes. Useful for multi-extruder prints with translucent materials or manual soluble support material.

projections.label: Interlocking beam layers
projections.tooltip: The height of the beams of the interlocking structure, measured in number of layers. Less layers is stronger, but more prone to defects.

projections.label: Interlocking beam width
projections.tooltip: The width of the interlocking structure beams.

projections.label: Use beam interlocking
projections.tooltip: Generate interlocking beam structure at the locations where different filaments touch. This improves the adhesion between filaments, especially models printed in different materials.

projections.label: Interlocking boundary avoidance
projections.tooltip: The distance from the outside of a model where interlocking structures will not be generated, measured in cells.

projections.label: Interlocking depth
projections.tooltip: The distance from the boundary between filaments to generate interlocking structure, measured in cells. Too few cells will result in poor adhesion.

projections.label: Interlocking direction
projections.tooltip: Orientation of interlock beams.

projections.label: Internal bridge infill direction
projections.tooltip:
Internal bridging angle override. If left to zero, the bridging angle will be calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided angle will be used for internal bridges. Use 180°for zero angle.

It is recommended to leave it at 0 unless there is a specific model need not to.

projections.label: Internal bridge density
projections.tooltip:
Controls the density (spacing) of internal bridge lines. 100% means solid bridge. Default is 100%.

Lower density internal bridges can help reduce top surface pillowing and improve internal bridge reliability as there is more space for air to circulate around the extruded bridge, improving its cooling speed.

This option works particularly well when combined with the second internal bridge over infill option, further improving internal bridging structure before solid infill is extruded.

projections.label: Internal bridges fan speed
projections.tooltip:
The part cooling fan speed used for all internal bridges. Set to -1 to use the overhang fan speed settings instead.

Reducing the internal bridges fan speed, compared to your regular fan speed, can help reduce part warping due to excessive cooling applied over a large surface for a prolonged period of time.

projections.label: Internal bridge flow ratio
projections.tooltip:
This value governs the thickness of the internal bridge layer. This is the first layer over sparse infill. Decrease this value slightly (for example 0.9) to improve surface quality over sparse infill.

The actual internal bridge flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the bridge flow ratio, the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

projections.label: Internal
projections.tooltip: Speed of internal bridges. If the value is expressed as a percentage, it will be calculated based on the bridge_speed. Default value is 150%.

projections.label: Internal solid infill
projections.tooltip: Acceleration of internal solid infill. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 100%), it will be calculated based on the default acceleration.

projections.label: Internal solid infill
projections.tooltip: Line width of internal solid infill. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

projections.label: Internal solid infill pattern
projections.tooltip: Line pattern of internal solid infill. if the detect narrow internal solid infill be enabled, the concentric pattern will be used for the small area.

projections.label: Internal solid infill
projections.tooltip: Speed of internal solid infill, not the top and bottom surface.

projections.label: Ironing angle
projections.tooltip: The angle ironing is done at. A negative number disables this function and uses the default method.

projections.label: Ironing fan speed
projections.tooltip:
This part cooling fan speed is applied when ironing. Setting this parameter to a lower than regular speed reduces possible nozzle clogging due to the low volumetric flow rate, making the interface smoother.
Set to -1 to disable it.

projections.label: Ironing flow
projections.tooltip: The amount of material to extrude during ironing. Relative to flow of normal layer height. Too high value results in overextrusion on the surface.

projections.label: Ironing inset
projections.tooltip: The distance to keep from the edges. A value of 0 sets this to half of the nozzle diameter.

projections.label: Ironing Pattern
projections.tooltip: The pattern that will be used when ironing.

projections.label: Ironing line spacing
projections.tooltip: The distance between the lines of ironing.

projections.label: Ironing speed
projections.tooltip: Print speed of ironing lines.

projections.label: Ironing Type
projections.tooltip: Ironing is using small flow to print on same height of surface again to make flat surface more smooth. This setting controls which layer being ironed

projections.label: Print infill first
projections.tooltip:
Order of wall/infill. When the tickbox is unchecked the walls are printed first, which works best in most cases.

Printing infill first may help with extreme overhangs as the walls have the neighbouring infill to adhere to. However, the infill will slightly push out the printed walls where it is attached to them, resulting in a worse external surface finish. It can also cause the infill to shine through the external surfaces of the part.

projections.label: Lateral lattice angle 1
projections.tooltip: The angle of the first set of Lateral lattice elements in the Z direction. Zero is vertical.

projections.label: Lateral lattice angle 2
projections.tooltip: The angle of the second set of Lateral lattice elements in the Z direction. Zero is vertical.

projections.label: Layer change G-code
projections.tooltip: This G-code is inserted at every layer change after the Z lift.

projections.label: Default
projections.tooltip: Default line width if other line widths are set to 0. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

projections.label: Local-Z mini wipe lines
projections.tooltip: Number of purge lines reserved for each runtime Local-Z wipe tower toolchange. Higher values improve cleanup but increase tower depth. Only used when Local-Z dithering and the prime tower are enabled.

projections.label: Long retraction when cut (beta)
projections.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retracting and cutting off the filament at a longer distance during changes to minimize purge. While this reduces flush significantly, it may also raise the risk of nozzle clogs or other printing problems.

projections.label: End G-code
projections.tooltip: End G-code when finishing the entire print.

projections.label: Filament load time
projections.tooltip: Time to load new filament when switch filament. It's usually applicable for single-extruder multi-material machines. For tool changers or multi-tool machines, it's typically 0. For statistics only.

projections.label: machine_max_acceleration_e
projections.tooltip: Maximum acceleration of the E axis

projections.label: machine_max_acceleration_extruding
projections.tooltip: Maximum acceleration for extruding (M204 P)

projections.label: machine_max_acceleration_retracting
projections.tooltip: Maximum acceleration for retracting (M204 R)

projections.label: machine_max_acceleration_travel
projections.tooltip: Maximum acceleration for travel (M204 T), it only applies to Marlin 2.

projections.label: machine_max_acceleration_x
projections.tooltip: Maximum acceleration of the X axis

projections.label: machine_max_acceleration_y
projections.tooltip: Maximum acceleration of the Y axis

projections.label: machine_max_acceleration_z
projections.tooltip: Maximum acceleration of the Z axis

projections.label: machine_max_jerk_e
projections.tooltip: Maximum jerk of the E axis

projections.label: machine_max_jerk_x
projections.tooltip: Maximum jerk of the X axis

projections.label: machine_max_jerk_y
projections.tooltip: Maximum jerk of the Y axis

projections.label: machine_max_jerk_z
projections.tooltip: Maximum jerk of the Z axis

projections.label: machine_max_junction_deviation
projections.tooltip: Maximum junction deviation (M205 J, only apply if JD > 0 for Marlin Firmware)

projections.label: machine_max_speed_e
projections.tooltip: Maximum speed of E axis

projections.label: machine_max_speed_x
projections.tooltip: Maximum speed of X axis

projections.label: machine_max_speed_y
projections.tooltip: Maximum speed of Y axis

projections.label: machine_max_speed_z
projections.tooltip: Maximum speed of Z axis

projections.label: machine_min_extruding_rate
projections.tooltip: Minimum speed for extruding (M205 S)

projections.label: machine_min_travel_rate
projections.tooltip: Minimum travel speed (M205 T)

projections.label: Pause G-code
projections.tooltip: This G-code will be used as a code for the pause print. Users can insert pause G-code in the G-code viewer.

projections.label: Start G-code
projections.tooltip: Start G-code when starting the entire print.

projections.label: Tool change time
projections.tooltip: Time taken to switch tools. It's usually applicable for tool changers or multi-tool machines. For single-extruder multi-material machines, it's typically 0. For statistics only.

projections.label: Filament unload time
projections.tooltip: Time to unload old filament when switch filament. It's usually applicable for single-extruder multi-material machines. For tool changers or multi-tool machines, it's typically 0. For statistics only.

projections.label: Make overhangs printable - Maximum angle
projections.tooltip: Maximum angle of overhangs to allow after making more steep overhangs printable.90° will not change the model at all and allow any overhang, while 0 will replace all overhangs with conical material.

projections.label: Make overhangs printable - Hole area
projections.tooltip: Maximum area of a hole in the base of the model before it's filled by conical material. A value of 0 will fill all the holes in the model base.

projections.label: Make overhangs printable
projections.tooltip: Modify the geometry to print overhangs without support material.

projections.label: Manual Filament Change
projections.tooltip: Enable this option to omit the custom Change filament G-code only at the beginning of the print. The tool change command (e.g., T0) will be skipped throughout the entire print. This is useful for manual multi-material printing, where we use M600/PAUSE to trigger the manual filament change action.

projections.label: Max bridge length
projections.tooltip: Max length of bridges that don't need support. Set it to 0 if you want all bridges to be supported, and set it to a very large value if you don't want any bridges to be supported.

projections.label: Max
projections.tooltip: The highest printable layer height for the extruder. Used to limit the maximum layer height when enable adaptive layer height.

projections.label: Max
projections.tooltip: Maximum speed of resonance avoidance.

projections.label: Avoid crossing walls - Max detour length
projections.tooltip: Maximum detour distance for avoiding crossing wall. Don't detour if the detour distance is larger than this value. Detour length could be specified either as an absolute value or as percentage (for example 50%) of a direct travel path. Zero to disable.

projections.label: Smoothing segment length
projections.tooltip:
A lower value results in smoother extrusion rate transitions. However, this results in a significantly larger G-code file and more instructions for the printer to process.

Default value of 3 works well for most cases. If your printer is stuttering, increase this value to reduce the number of adjustments made.

Allowed values: 0.5-5

projections.label: Extrusion rate smoothing
projections.tooltip:
This parameter smooths out sudden extrusion rate changes that happen when the printer transitions from printing a high flow (high speed/larger width) extrusion to a lower flow (lower speed/smaller width) extrusion and vice versa.

It defines the maximum rate by which the extruded volumetric flow in mm³/s can change over time. Higher values mean higher extrusion rate changes are allowed, resulting in faster speed transitions.

A value of 0 disables the feature.

For a high speed, high flow direct drive printer (like the Bambu lab or Voron) this value is usually not needed. However it can provide some marginal benefit in certain cases where feature speeds vary greatly. For example, when there are aggressive slowdowns due to overhangs. In these cases a high value of around 300-350 mm³/s² is recommended as this allows for just enough smoothing to assist pressure advance achieve a smoother flow transition.

For slower printers without pressure advance, the value should be set much lower. A value of 10-15 mm³/s² is a good starting point for direct drive extruders and 5-10 mm³/s² for Bowden style.

This feature is known as Pressure Equalizer in Prusa slicer.

Note: this parameter disables arc fitting.

projections.label: Minimum wall width
projections.tooltip: Width of the wall that will replace thin features (according to the Minimum feature size) of the model. If the Minimum wall width is thinner than the thickness of the feature, the wall will become as thick as the feature itself. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.

projections.label: Minimum feature size
projections.tooltip: Minimum thickness of thin features. Model features that are thinner than this value will not be printed, while features thicker than than this value will be widened to the minimum wall width. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.

projections.label: Min
projections.tooltip: The lowest printable layer height for the extruder. Used to limit the minimum layer height when enable adaptive layer height.

projections.label: Minimum wall length
projections.tooltip:
Adjust this value to prevent short, unclosed walls from being printed, which could increase print time. Higher values remove more and longer walls.

NOTE: Bottom and top surfaces will not be affected by this value to prevent visual gaps on the outside of the model. Adjust 'One wall threshold' in the Advanced settings below to adjust the sensitivity of what is considered a top-surface. 'One wall threshold' is only visible if this setting is set above the default value of 0.5, or if single-wall top surfaces is enabled.

projections.label: Min
projections.tooltip: Minimum speed of resonance avoidance.

projections.label: Skirt minimum extrusion length
projections.tooltip:
Minimum filament extrusion length in mm when printing the skirt. Zero means this feature is disabled.

Using a non-zero value is useful if the printer is set up to print without a prime line.
Final number of loops is not taking into account while arranging or validating objects distance. Increase loop number in such case.

projections.label: One wall threshold
projections.tooltip:
If a top surface has to be printed and it's partially covered by another layer, it won't be considered at a top layer where its width is below this value. This can be useful to not let the 'one perimeter on top' trigger on surface that should be covered only by perimeters. This value can be a mm or a % of the perimeter extrusion width.
Warning: If enabled, artifacts can be created if you have some thin features on the next layer, like letters. Set this setting to 0 to remove these artifacts.

projections.label: Minimum sparse infill threshold
projections.tooltip: Sparse infill area which is smaller than threshold value is replaced by internal solid infill.

projections.label: Dithering cadence height A
projections.tooltip:
Layer height contribution of component A for dithering virtual filaments. Set to 0 to use normal 1-layer A / 1-layer B alternation.

Detailed mixed filament setting explanations will be published once the project wiki is available.

projections.label: Dithering cadence height B
projections.tooltip:
Layer height contribution of component B for dithering virtual filaments. Set to 0 to use normal 1-layer A / 1-layer B alternation.

Detailed mixed filament setting explanations will be published once the project wiki is available.

projections.label: Advanced dithering
projections.tooltip:
Distribute mixed filament layer-cycle cadence using an advanced ordered dithering pattern instead of a simple contiguous A-then-B run. This can reduce visible striping for some hues.

This is an even more experimental mode and the perceived color may differ from normal dithering for the same filament pair and ratio.

Detailed mixed filament setting explanations will be published once the project wiki is available.

projections.label: Enable mixed filament bias
projections.tooltip:
Show and apply the per-row mixed filament Bias control.

When enabled, the selected filament in a mixed pair is recessed slightly so the other component becomes more visible.

Bias is ignored for grouped wall patterns, same-layer pointillisme, and Local Z dithering.

projections.label: Mixed filament custom definitions
projections.tooltip:
Serialized custom mixed filament rows.

Detailed mixed filament setting explanations will be published once the project wiki is available.

projections.label: Height-weighted cadence
projections.tooltip:
Enable height-weighted cadence for mixed filaments. Limitation: only one height-weighted mixed color should be present at a given Z plane, because independent per-color layer heights are not supported and the resulting layer height applies to the whole plane. When disabled, layer-cycle cadence is used.

Detailed mixed filament setting explanations will be published once the project wiki is available.

projections.label: Local-Z lower height bound
projections.tooltip:
Lower bound used when Local-Z mixed-filament dithering chooses per-color sublayer heights.

Smaller values let Local-Z use thinner sublayers for a color when needed.

Detailed mixed filament setting explanations will be published once the project wiki is available.

projections.label: Local-Z upper height bound
projections.tooltip:
Upper bound used when Local-Z mixed-filament dithering chooses per-color sublayer heights.

Larger values let Local-Z use thicker sublayers for a color when needed.

Detailed mixed filament setting explanations will be published once the project wiki is available.

projections.label: Pointillisme line gap
projections.tooltip:
Optional non-extruded spacing between adjacent pointillisme segments. Increase carefully to improve separation and print quality.

Warning: Same-layer pointillisme is extremely experimental and may produce unusable results.

projections.label: Pointillisme pixel size
projections.tooltip:
Length of one pointillisme segment along an extrusion path for same-layer pointillisme mode. Set to 0 to use automatic nozzle-based sizing.

Warning: Same-layer pointillisme is extremely experimental and may produce unusable results.

projections.label: Collapse same-color mixed regions
projections.tooltip:
Merge ordinary mixed-filament painted regions into a single area when they resolve to the same physical filament on a layer.

This improves continuity for adjacent same-color areas.

Subdivide Mix Layer disables this behavior, and gradient mixed regions also bypass it because they use the Local-Z pipeline.

projections.label: Selective Expansion contraction
projections.tooltip:
XY offset applied to mixed-filament painted regions before region assignment.

Positive values contract the mixed zone inward. Negative values expand it outward.

This applies to mixed filament usage in layer cadence, height cadence, same-layer pointillisme, and local Z dithering.

projections.label: Interlocking depth of a segmented region
projections.tooltip: Interlocking depth of a segmented region. It will be ignored if "mmu_segmented_region_max_width" is zero or if "mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth" is bigger than "mmu_segmented_region_max_width". Zero disables this feature.

projections.label: Maximum width of a segmented region
projections.tooltip: Maximum width of a segmented region. Zero disables this feature.

projections.label: Configuration notes
projections.tooltip: You can put here your personal notes. This text will be added to the G-code header comments.

projections.label: Nozzle diameter
projections.tooltip: The diameter of nozzle.

projections.label: Nozzle height
projections.tooltip: The height of nozzle tip.

projections.label: Nozzle HRC
projections.tooltip: The nozzle's hardness. Zero means no checking for nozzle's hardness during slicing.

projections.label: Initial layer
projections.tooltip: Nozzle temperature for printing initial layer when using this filament.

projections.label: Other layers
projections.tooltip: Nozzle temperature for layers after the initial one.

projections.label: Nozzle type
projections.tooltip: The metallic material of nozzle. This determines the abrasive resistance of nozzle, and what kind of filament can be printed.

projections.label: Nozzle volume
projections.tooltip: Volume of nozzle between the cutter and the end of nozzle.

projections.label: Only one wall on first layer
projections.tooltip: Use only one wall on first layer, to give more space to the bottom infill pattern.

projections.label: Only one wall on top surfaces
projections.tooltip: Use only one wall on flat top surfaces, to give more space to the top infill pattern.

projections.label: Enable
projections.tooltip: This option will drop the temperature of the inactive extruders to prevent oozing.

projections.label: The number of other layers print sequence
Outer wall
projections.tooltip: Acceleration of outer walls.

projections.label: Outer wall
projections.tooltip: Acceleration of outer wall. Using a lower value can improve quality.

projections.label: Outer wall
projections.tooltip: Jerk of outer walls.

projections.label: Outer wall
projections.tooltip: Line width of outer wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

projections.label: Outer wall
projections.tooltip: Speed of outer wall which is outermost and visible. It's used to be slower than inner wall speed to get better quality.

projections.label: Overhangs and external bridges fan speed
projections.tooltip:
Use this part cooling fan speed when printing bridges or overhang walls with an overhang threshold that exceeds the value set in the 'Overhangs cooling threshold' parameter above. Increasing the cooling specifically for overhangs and bridges can improve the overall print quality of these features.

Please note, this fan speed is clamped on the lower end by the minimum fan speed threshold set above. It is also adjusted upwards up to the maximum fan speed threshold when the minimum layer time threshold is not met.

projections.label: Overhang cooling activation threshold
projections.tooltip: When the overhang exceeds this specified threshold, force the cooling fan to run at the 'Overhang Fan Speed' set below. This threshold is expressed as a percentage, indicating the portion of each line's width that is unsupported by the layer beneath it. Setting this value to 0% forces the cooling fan to run for all outer walls, regardless of the overhang degree.

projections.label: Reverse only internal perimeters
projections.tooltip:
Apply the reverse perimeters logic only on internal perimeters.

This setting greatly reduces part stresses as they are now distributed in alternating directions. This should reduce part warping while also maintaining external wall quality. This feature can be very useful for warp prone material, like ABS/ASA, and also for elastic filaments, like TPU and Silk PLA. It can also help reduce warping on floating regions over supports.

For this setting to be the most effective, it is recommended to set the Reverse Threshold to 0 so that all internal walls print in alternating directions on even layers irrespective of their overhang degree.

projections.label: Reverse threshold
projections.tooltip:
Number of mm the overhang need to be for the reversal to be considered useful. Can be a % of the perimeter width.
Value 0 enables reversal on every even layers regardless.
When Detect overhang wall is not enabled, this option is ignored and reversal happens on every even layers regardless.

projections.label: Reverse on even
projections.tooltip:
Extrude perimeters that have a part over an overhang in the reverse direction on even layers. This alternating pattern can drastically improve steep overhangs.

This setting can also help reduce part warping due to the reduction of stresses in the part walls.

projections.label: Filament parking position
projections.tooltip: Distance of the extruder tip from the position where the filament is parked when unloaded. This should match the value in printer firmware.

projections.label: Pellet flow coefficient
projections.tooltip:
Pellet flow coefficient is empirically derived and allows for volume calculation for pellet printers.

Internally it is converted to filament_diameter. All other volume calculations remain the same.

filament_diameter = sqrt( (4 * pellet_flow_coefficient) / PI )

projections.label: Pellet Modded Printer
projections.tooltip: Enable this option if your printer uses pellets instead of filaments.

projections.label: Post-processing Scripts
projections.tooltip: If you want to process the output G-code through custom scripts, just list their absolute paths here. Separate multiple scripts with a semicolon. Scripts will be passed the absolute path to the G-code file as the first argument, and they can access the Snapmaker Orca config settings by reading environment variables.

projections.label: Precise wall
projections.tooltip: Improve shell precision by adjusting outer wall spacing. This also improves layer consistency. NOTE: This option will be ignored for outer-inner or inner-outer-inner wall sequences.

projections.label: Precise Z height
projections.tooltip: Enable this to get precise z height of object after slicing. It will get the precise object height by fine-tuning the layer heights of the last few layers. Note that this is an experimental parameter.

projections.label: Preheat steps
projections.tooltip: Insert multiple preheat commands (e.g. M104.1). Only useful for Prusa XL. For other printers, please set it to 1.

projections.label: Preheat time
projections.tooltip: To reduce the waiting time after tool change, Orca can preheat the next tool while the current tool is still in use. This setting specifies the time in seconds to preheat the next tool. Orca will insert a M104 command to preheat the tool in advance.

projections.label: Pressure advance
projections.tooltip: Pressure advance (Klipper) AKA Linear advance factor (Marlin).

projections.label: Max chamfer width
projections.tooltip: Maximum width of the chamfer zone measured from the tower perimeter. The brim will reduce within this distance. Larger values create a more gradual taper but take more layers to complete.

projections.label: Brim chamfer
projections.tooltip: Enable gradual layer-by-layer reduction of the brim around the prime tower. This creates a chamfered/tapered effect, reducing material usage while maintaining first layer adhesion.

projections.label: Brim width
projections.tooltip: Width of the brim.

projections.label: Width
projections.tooltip: Width of the prime tower.

projections.label: Prime volume
projections.tooltip: The volume of material to prime extruder on tower.

projections.label: Flow ratio
projections.tooltip:
The material may have volumetric change after switching between molten and crystalline states. This setting changes all extrusion flow of this filament in G-code proportionally. The recommended value range is between 0.95 and 1.05. You may be able to tune this value to get a nice flat surface if there is slight overflow or underflow.

The final object flow ratio is this value multiplied by the filament flow ratio.

projections.label: Intra-layer order
projections.tooltip: Print order within a single layer.

projections.label: Print sequence
projections.tooltip: Print sequence, layer by layer or object by object.

projections.label: Printer type
projections.tooltip: Type of the printer.

projections.label: Printer notes
projections.tooltip: You can put your notes regarding the printer here.

projections.label: Printer structure
projections.tooltip: The physical arrangement and components of a printing device.

projections.label: Between Object G-code
projections.tooltip: Insert G-code between objects. This parameter will only come into effect when you print your models object by object.

projections.label: Purge in prime tower
projections.tooltip: Purge remaining filament into prime tower.

projections.label: Raft contact Z distance
projections.tooltip: Z gap between object and raft. Ignored for soluble interface.

projections.label: Raft expansion
projections.tooltip: Expand all raft layers in XY plane.

projections.label: Initial layer density
projections.tooltip: Density of the first raft or support layer.

projections.label: Initial layer expansion
projections.tooltip: Expand the first raft or support layer to improve bed plate adhesion.

projections.label: Raft layers
projections.tooltip: Object will be raised by this number of support layers. Use this function to avoid warping when printing ABS.

projections.label: Ramming line width ratio
projections.tooltip: This is used to decide the line width of wipe tower when ramming, ramming line width = [this ratio] * extruder * 1.25

projections.label: Pressure advance value when ramming
projections.tooltip: Set_Pressure_advance [this value] when ramming on wipe tower

projections.label: Avoid crossing walls
projections.tooltip: Detour and avoid to travel across wall which may cause blob on surface

projections.label: Keep fan always on
projections.tooltip: Enabling this setting means that the part cooling fan will never stop completely and will run at least at minimum speed to reduce the frequency of starting and stopping.

projections.label: Reduce infill retraction
projections.tooltip: Don't retract when the travel is in infill area absolutely. That means the oozing can't been seen. This can reduce times of retraction for complex model and save printing time, but make slicing and G-code generating slower.

projections.label: Required nozzle HRC
projections.tooltip: Minimum HRC of nozzle required to print the filament. Zero means no checking of nozzle's HRC.

projections.label: Resolution
projections.tooltip: The G-code path is generated after simplifying the contour of models to avoid too many points and G-code lines. Smaller value means higher resolution and more time to slice.

projections.label: Resonance avoidance
projections.tooltip:
By reducing the speed of the outer wall to avoid the resonance zone of the printer, ringing on the surface of the model are avoided.
Please turn this option off when testing ringing.

projections.label: Retract amount before wipe
projections.tooltip: The length of fast retraction before wipe, relative to retraction length.

projections.label: Z-hop lower boundary
