projections.tooltip: Z-hop will only come into effect when Z is above this value and is below the parameter: "Z-hop upper boundary".

projections.label: Only lift Z above
projections.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place above the specified absolute Z.

projections.label: Z-hop upper boundary
projections.tooltip: If this value is positive, Z-hop will only come into effect when Z is above the parameter: "Z-hop lower boundary" and is below this value.

projections.label: Only lift Z below
projections.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place below the specified absolute Z.

projections.label: On surfaces
projections.tooltip: Enforce Z-Hop behavior. This setting is impacted by the above settings (Only lift Z above/below).

projections.label: Extra length on restart
projections.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after changing tool, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament.

projections.label: Extra length on restart
projections.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after the travel move, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament. This setting is rarely needed.

projections.label: Retract when change layer
projections.tooltip: Force a retraction when changes layer.

projections.label: Retraction distance when cut
projections.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retraction length before cutting off during filament change.

projections.label: Length
projections.tooltip: Some amount of material in extruder is pulled back to avoid ooze during long travel. Set zero to disable retraction.

projections.label: Travel distance threshold
projections.tooltip: Only trigger retraction when the travel distance is longer than this threshold.

projections.label: Retraction Speed
projections.tooltip: Speed for retracting filament from the nozzle.

projections.label: Role base wipe speed
projections.tooltip: The wipe speed is determined by the speed of the current extrusion role. e.g. if a wipe action is executed immediately following an outer wall extrusion, the speed of the outer wall extrusion will be utilized for the wipe action.

projections.label: Scan first layer
projections.tooltip: Enable this to enable the camera on printer to check the quality of first layer.

projections.label: Conditional angle threshold
projections.tooltip:
This option sets the threshold angle for applying a conditional scarf joint seam.
If the maximum angle within the perimeter loop exceeds this value (indicating the absence of sharp corners), a scarf joint seam will be used. The default value is 155°.

projections.label: Scarf joint flow ratio
projections.tooltip: This factor affects the amount of material for scarf joints.

projections.label: Scarf joint speed
projections.tooltip: This option sets the printing speed for scarf joints. It is recommended to print scarf joints at a slow speed (less than 100 mm/s). It's also advisable to enable 'Extrusion rate smoothing' if the set speed varies significantly from the speed of the outer or inner walls. If the speed specified here is higher than the speed of the outer or inner walls, the printer will default to the slower of the two speeds. When specified as a percentage (e.g., 80%), the speed is calculated based on the respective outer or inner wall speed. The default value is set to 100%.

projections.label: Conditional overhang threshold
projections.tooltip: This option determines the overhang threshold for the application of scarf joint seams. If the unsupported portion of the perimeter is less than this threshold, scarf joint seams will be applied. The default threshold is set at 40% of the external wall's width. Due to performance considerations, the degree of overhang is estimated.

projections.label: Seam gap
projections.tooltip:
In order to reduce the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, the loop is interrupted and shortened by a specified amount.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current extruder diameter. The default value for this parameter is 10%.

projections.label: Seam position
projections.tooltip: The start position to print each part of outer wall.

projections.label: Conditional scarf joint
projections.tooltip: Apply scarf joints only to smooth perimeters where traditional seams do not conceal the seams at sharp corners effectively.

projections.label: Scarf around entire wall
projections.tooltip: The scarf extends to the entire length of the wall.

projections.label: Scarf joint for inner walls
projections.tooltip: Use scarf joint for inner walls as well.

projections.label: Scarf length
projections.tooltip: Length of the scarf. Setting this parameter to zero effectively disables the scarf.

projections.label: Scarf start height
projections.tooltip:
Start height of the scarf.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current layer height. The default value for this parameter is 0.

projections.label: Scarf steps
projections.tooltip: Minimum number of segments of each scarf.

projections.label: Scarf joint seam (beta)
projections.tooltip: Use scarf joint to minimize seam visibility and increase seam strength.

projections.label: Supports silent mode
projections.tooltip: Whether the machine supports silent mode in which machine use lower acceleration to print.

projections.label: Prime all printing extruders
projections.tooltip: If enabled, all printing extruders will be primed at the front edge of the print bed at the start of the print.

projections.label: Single Extruder Multi Material
projections.tooltip: Use single nozzle to print multi filament.

projections.label: Single loop after first layer
projections.tooltip: Limits the skirt/draft shield loops to one wall after the first layer. This is useful, on occasion, to conserve filament but may cause the draft shield/skirt to warp / crack.

projections.label: Skeleton infill density
projections.tooltip: The remaining part of the model contour after removing a certain depth from the surface is called the skeleton. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section. When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skeleton densities, their skeleton areas will develop overlapping sections. Default is as same as infill density.

projections.label: Skeleton line width
projections.tooltip: Adjust the line width of the selected skeleton paths.

projections.label: Skin infill density
projections.tooltip: The portion of the model's outer surface within a certain depth range is called the skin. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section. When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skin densities, this area will not be split into two separate regions. Default is as same as infill density.

projections.label: Skin infill depth
projections.tooltip: The parameter sets the depth of skin.

projections.label: Skin line width
projections.tooltip: Adjust the line width of the selected skin paths.

projections.label: Skirt distance
projections.tooltip: The distance from the skirt to the brim or the object.

projections.label: Skirt height
projections.tooltip: How many layers of skirt. Usually only one layer.

projections.label: Skirt loops
projections.tooltip: Number of loops for the skirt. Zero means disabling skirt.

projections.label: Skirt speed
projections.tooltip: Speed of skirt, in mm/s. Zero means use default layer extrusion speed.

projections.label: Skirt start point
projections.tooltip: Angle from the object center to skirt start point. Zero is the most right position, counter clockwise is positive angle.

projections.label: Skirt type
projections.tooltip: Combined - single skirt for all objects, Per object - individual object skirt.

projections.label: Slice gap closing radius
projections.tooltip: Cracks smaller than 2x gap closing radius are being filled during the triangle mesh slicing. The gap closing operation may reduce the final print resolution, therefore it is advisable to keep the value reasonably low.

projections.label: Slicing Mode
projections.tooltip: Use "Even-odd" for 3DLabPrint airplane models. Use "Close holes" to close all holes in the model.

projections.label: Slow printing down for better layer cooling
projections.tooltip: Enable this option to slow printing speed down to make the final layer time not shorter than the layer time threshold in "Max fan speed threshold", so that layer can be cooled for longer time. This can improve the cooling quality for needle and small details.

projections.label: Layer time
projections.tooltip: The printing speed in exported G-code will be slowed down when the estimated layer time is shorter than this value in order to get better cooling for these layers.

projections.label: Number of slow layers
projections.tooltip: The first few layers are printed slower than normal. The speed is gradually increased in a linear fashion over the specified number of layers.

projections.label: Min print speed
projections.tooltip: The minimum print speed to which the printer slows down to maintain the minimum layer time defined above when the slowdown for better layer cooling is enabled.

projections.label: Slow down for curled perimeters
projections.tooltip:
Enable this option to slow down printing in areas where perimeters may have curled upwards. For example, additional slowdown will be applied when printing overhangs on sharp corners like the front of the Benchy hull, reducing curling which compounds over multiple layers.

It is generally recommended to have this option switched on unless your printer cooling is powerful enough or the print speed slow enough that perimeter curling does not happen. If printing with a high external perimeter speed, this parameter may introduce slight artifacts when slowing down due to the large variance in print speeds. If you notice artifacts, ensure your pressure advance is tuned correctly.

Note: When this option is enabled, overhang perimeters are treated like overhangs, meaning the overhang speed is applied even if the overhanging perimeter is part of a bridge. For example, when the perimeters are 100% overhanging, with no wall supporting them from underneath, the 100% overhang speed will be applied.

projections.label: Flow Compensation Model
projections.tooltip: Flow Compensation Model, used to adjust the flow for small infill areas. The model is expressed as a comma separated pair of values for extrusion length and flow correction factor. Each pair is on a separate line, followed by a semicolon, in the following format: "1.234, 5.678;"

projections.label: Small area flow compensation (beta)
projections.tooltip: Enable flow compensation for small infill areas.

projections.label: Small perimeters
projections.tooltip: This separate setting will affect the speed of perimeters having radius <= small_perimeter_threshold (usually holes). If expressed as percentage (for example: 80%) it will be calculated on the outer wall speed setting above. Set to zero for auto.

projections.label: Small perimeters threshold
projections.tooltip: This sets the threshold for small perimeter length. Default threshold is 0mm.

projections.label: Solid infill direction
projections.tooltip: Angle for solid infill pattern, which controls the start or main direction of line.

projections.label: Solid infill
projections.tooltip: Filament to print solid infill.

projections.label: Solid infill rotation template
projections.tooltip: This parameter adds a rotation of solid infill direction to each layer according to the specified template. The template is a comma-separated list of angles in degrees, e.g. '0,90'. The first angle is applied to the first layer, the second angle to the second layer, and so on. If there are more layers than angles, the angles will be repeated. Note that not all solid infill patterns support rotation.

projections.label: Sparse infill
projections.tooltip: Acceleration of sparse infill. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 100%), it will be calculated based on the default acceleration.

projections.label: Sparse infill density
projections.tooltip: Density of internal sparse infill, 100% turns all sparse infill into solid infill and internal solid infill pattern will be used.

projections.label: Infill
projections.tooltip: Filament to print internal sparse infill.

projections.label: Sparse infill
projections.tooltip: Line width of internal sparse infill. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

projections.label: Sparse infill pattern
projections.tooltip: Line pattern for internal sparse infill.

projections.label: Sparse infill rotation template
projections.tooltip: Rotate the sparse infill direction per layer using a template of angles. Enter comma-separated degrees (e.g., '0,30,60,90'). Angles are applied in order by layer and repeat when the list ends. Advanced syntax is supported: '+5' rotates +5° every layer; '+5#5' rotates +5° every 5 layers. See the Wiki for details. When a template is set, the standard infill direction setting is ignored. Note: some infill patterns (e.g., Gyroid) control rotation themselves; use with care.

projections.label: Sparse infill
projections.tooltip: Speed of internal sparse infill.

projections.label: Spiral finishing flow ratio
projections.tooltip: Sets the finishing flow ratio while ending the spiral. Normally the spiral transition scales the flow ratio from 100% to 0% during the last loop which can in some cases lead to under extrusion at the end of the spiral.

projections.label: Max XY Smoothing
projections.tooltip: Maximum distance to move points in XY to try to achieve a smooth spiral. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over nozzle diameter.

projections.label: Smooth Spiral
projections.tooltip: Smooth Spiral smooths out X and Y moves as well, resulting in no visible seam at all, even in the XY directions on walls that are not vertical.

projections.label: Spiral vase
projections.tooltip: Spiralize smooths out the z moves of the outer contour. And turns a solid model into a single walled print with solid bottom layers. The final generated model has no seam.

projections.label: Spiral starting flow ratio
projections.tooltip: Sets the starting flow ratio while transitioning from the last bottom layer to the spiral. Normally the spiral transition scales the flow ratio from 0% to 100% during the first loop which can in some cases lead to under extrusion at the start of the spiral.

projections.label: Staggered inner seams
projections.tooltip: This option causes the inner seams to be shifted backwards based on their depth, forming a zigzag pattern.

projections.label: Temperature variation
projections.tooltip: Temperature difference to be applied when an extruder is not active. The value is not used when 'idle_temperature' in filament settings is set to non-zero value.

projections.label: Start end points
projections.tooltip: The start and end points which is from cutter area to garbage can.

projections.label: Initial layer
projections.tooltip: Bed temperature of the initial layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Cool Plate SuperTack.

projections.label: Other layers
projections.tooltip: Bed temperature for layers except the initial one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Cool Plate SuperTack.

projections.label: Support air filtration
projections.tooltip:
Enable this if printer support air filtration
G-code command: M106 P3 S(0-255)

projections.label: Pattern angle
projections.tooltip: Use this setting to rotate the support pattern on the horizontal plane.

projections.label: Base pattern spacing
projections.tooltip: Spacing between support lines.

projections.label: Base pattern
projections.tooltip: Line pattern of support.

projections.label: Bottom interface spacing
projections.tooltip: Spacing of bottom interface lines. Zero means solid interface.

projections.label: Bottom Z distance
projections.tooltip: The Z gap between the bottom support interface and object.

projections.label: Support control chamber temperature
projections.tooltip:
This option is enabled if machine support controlling chamber temperature
G-code command: M141 S(0-255)

projections.label: Support critical regions only
projections.tooltip: Only create support for critical regions including sharp tail, cantilever, etc.

projections.label: Normal Support expansion
projections.tooltip: Expand (+) or shrink (-) the horizontal span of normal support.

projections.label: Support/raft base
projections.tooltip: Filament to print support base and raft. "Default" means no specific filament for support and current filament is used.

projections.label: Bottom interface layers
projections.tooltip: Number of bottom interface layers.

projections.label: Support/raft interface
projections.tooltip: Filament to print support interface. "Default" means no specific filament for support interface and current filament is used.

projections.label: Interface use loop pattern
projections.tooltip: Cover the top contact layer of the supports with loops. Disabled by default.

projections.label: Avoid interface filament for base
projections.tooltip: Avoid using support interface filament to print support base if possible.

projections.label: Interface pattern
projections.tooltip: Line pattern of support interface. Default pattern for non-soluble support interface is Rectilinear, while default pattern for soluble support interface is Concentric.

projections.label: Top interface spacing
projections.tooltip:
Spacing of interface lines. Zero means solid interface.
Force using solid interface when support ironing is enabled.

projections.label: Support interface
projections.tooltip: Speed of support interface.

projections.label: Top interface layers
projections.tooltip: Number of top interface layers.

projections.label: Support Ironing flow
projections.tooltip: The amount of material to extrude during ironing. Relative to flow of normal support interface layer height. Too high value results in overextrusion on the surface.

projections.label: Support Ironing Pattern
projections.tooltip: The pattern that will be used when ironing.

projections.label: Support Ironing line spacing
projections.tooltip: The distance between the lines of ironing.

projections.label: Ironing Support Interface
projections.tooltip: Ironing is using small flow to print on same height of support interface again to make it more smooth. This setting controls whether support interface being ironed. When enabled, support interface will be extruded as solid too.

projections.label: Support
projections.tooltip: Line width of support. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

projections.label: Support interface fan speed
projections.tooltip:
This part cooling fan speed is applied when printing support interfaces. Setting this parameter to a higher than regular speed reduces the layer binding strength between supports and the supported part, making them easier to separate.
Set to -1 to disable it.
This setting is overridden by disable_fan_first_layers.

projections.label: Support multi bed types
projections.tooltip: Enable this option if you want to use multiple bed types.

projections.label: Support/object first layer gap
projections.tooltip: XY separation between an object and its support at the first layer.

projections.label: Support/object xy distance
projections.tooltip: XY separation between an object and its support.

projections.label: On build plate only
projections.tooltip: Don't create support on model surface, only on build plate.

projections.label: Remove small overhangs
projections.tooltip: Remove small overhangs that possibly need no supports.

projections.label: Support
projections.tooltip: Speed of support.

projections.label: Style
projections.tooltip:
Style and shape of the support. For normal support, projecting the supports into a regular grid will create more stable supports (default), while snug support towers will save material and reduce object scarring.
For tree support, slim and organic style will merge branches more aggressively and save a lot of material (default organic), while hybrid style will create similar structure to normal support under large flat overhangs.

projections.label: Threshold angle
projections.tooltip: Support will be generated for overhangs whose slope angle is below the threshold.

projections.label: Threshold overlap
projections.tooltip: If threshold angle is zero, support will be generated for overhangs whose overlap is below the threshold. The smaller this value is, the steeper the overhang that can be printed without support.

projections.label: Top Z distance
projections.tooltip: The Z gap between the top support interface and object.

projections.label: Type
projections.tooltip: Normal (auto) and Tree (auto) are used to generate support automatically. If Normal (manual) or Tree (manual) is selected, only support enforcers are generated.

projections.label: Symmetric infill Y axis
projections.tooltip: If the model has two parts that are symmetric about the Y axis, and you want these parts to have symmetric textures, please click this option on one of the parts.

projections.label: Softening temperature
projections.tooltip: The material softens at this temperature, so when the bed temperature is equal to or greater than this, it's highly recommended to open the front door and/or remove the upper glass to avoid clogging.

projections.label: Custom G-code
projections.tooltip: This G-code will be used as a custom code.

projections.label: Initial layer
projections.tooltip: Bed temperature of the initial layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Textured Cool Plate.

projections.label: Other layers
projections.tooltip: Bed temperature for layers except the initial one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Textured Cool Plate.

projections.label: Initial layer
projections.tooltip: Bed temperature of the initial layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Textured PEI Plate.

projections.label: Other layers
projections.tooltip: Bed temperature for layers except the initial one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Textured PEI Plate.

projections.label: Thick external bridges
projections.tooltip: If enabled, bridges are more reliable, can bridge longer distances, but may look worse. If disabled, bridges look better but are reliable just for shorter bridged distances.

projections.label: Thick internal bridges
projections.tooltip: If enabled, thick internal bridges will be used. It's usually recommended to have this feature turned on. However, consider turning it off if you are using large nozzles.

projections.label: small thumb
projections.tooltip: first small thumb

projections.label: big thumb
projections.tooltip: first big thumb

projections.label: Format of G-code thumbnails
projections.tooltip: Format of G-code thumbnails: PNG for best quality, JPG for smallest size, QOI for low memory firmware.

projections.label: G-code thumbnails
projections.tooltip: Picture sizes to be stored into a .gcode and .sl1 / .sl1s files, in the following format: "XxY, XxY, ..."

projections.label: Time cost
projections.tooltip: The printer cost per hour.

projections.label: Timelapse
projections.tooltip: If smooth or traditional mode is selected, a timelapse video will be generated for each print. After each layer is printed, a snapshot is taken with the chamber camera. All of these snapshots are composed into a timelapse video when printing completes. If smooth mode is selected, the toolhead will move to the excess chute after each layer is printed and then take a snapshot. Since the melt filament may leak from the nozzle during the process of taking a snapshot, prime tower is required for smooth mode to wipe nozzle.

projections.label: Wait for the temperature when changing tools
projections.tooltip: It will use the M109 instead of M104 T[target] after changing tools if this is set to true

projections.label: Top/Bottom solid infill/wall overlap
projections.tooltip: Top solid infill area is enlarged slightly to overlap with wall for better bonding and to minimize the appearance of pinholes where the top infill meets the walls. A value of 25-30% is a good starting point, minimizing the appearance of pinholes. The percentage value is relative to line width of sparse infill.

projections.label: Top shell layers
projections.tooltip: This is the number of solid layers of top shell, including the top surface layer. When the thickness calculated by this value is thinner than top shell thickness, the top shell layers will be increased.

projections.label: Top shell thickness
projections.tooltip: The number of top solid layers is increased when slicing if the thickness calculated by top shell layers is thinner than this value. This can avoid having too thin shell when layer height is small. 0 means that this setting is disabled and thickness of top shell is absolutely determined by top shell layers.

projections.label: Top surface flow ratio
projections.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for top solid infill. You can decrease it slightly to have smooth surface finish.

The actual top surface flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

projections.label: Top surface
projections.tooltip: Acceleration of top surface infill. Using a lower value may improve top surface quality.

projections.label: Top surface density
projections.tooltip: Density of top surface layer. A value of 100% creates a fully solid, smooth top layer. Reducing this value results in a textured top surface, according to the chosen top surface pattern. A value of 0% will result in only the walls on the top layer being created. Intended for aesthetic or functional purposes, not to fix issues such as over-extrusion.

projections.label: Top surface
projections.tooltip: Jerk for top surface.

projections.label: Top surface
projections.tooltip: Line width for top surfaces. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

projections.label: Top surface pattern
projections.tooltip: Line pattern of top surface infill.

projections.label: Top surface
projections.tooltip: Speed of top surface infill which is solid.

projections.label: Travel
projections.tooltip: Acceleration of travel moves.

projections.label: Travel
projections.tooltip: Jerk for travel.

projections.label: Traveling angle
projections.tooltip: Traveling angle for Slope and Spiral Z-hop type. Setting it to 90° results in Normal Lift.

projections.label: Travel
projections.tooltip: Speed of travel which is faster and without extrusion.

projections.label: Adaptive layer height
projections.tooltip: Enabling this option means the height of tree support layer except the first will be automatically calculated.

projections.label: Preferred Branch Angle
projections.tooltip: The preferred angle of the branches, when they do not have to avoid the model. Use a lower angle to make them more vertical and more stable. Use a higher angle for branches to merge faster.

projections.label: Auto brim width
projections.tooltip: Enabling this option means the width of the brim for tree support will be automatically calculated.

projections.label: Tree support branch angle
projections.tooltip: This setting determines the maximum overhang angle that the branches of tree support are allowed to make. If the angle is increased, the branches can be printed more horizontally, allowing them to reach farther.

projections.label: Tree support branch angle
projections.tooltip: This setting determines the maximum overhang angle that the branches of tree support are allowed to make. If the angle is increased, the branches can be printed more horizontally, allowing them to reach farther.

projections.label: Branch Diameter Angle
projections.tooltip: The angle of the branches' diameter as they gradually become thicker towards the bottom. An angle of 0 will cause the branches to have uniform thickness over their length. A bit of an angle can increase stability of the organic support.

projections.label: Tree support branch diameter
projections.tooltip: This setting determines the initial diameter of support nodes.

projections.label: Tree support branch diameter
projections.tooltip: This setting determines the initial diameter of support nodes.

projections.label: Tree support branch distance
projections.tooltip: This setting determines the distance between neighboring tree support nodes.

projections.label: Tree support branch distance
projections.tooltip: This setting determines the distance between neighboring tree support nodes.

projections.label: Tree support brim width
projections.tooltip: Distance from tree branch to the outermost brim line.

projections.label: Tip Diameter
projections.tooltip: Branch tip diameter for organic supports.

projections.label: Branch Density
projections.tooltip: Adjusts the density of the support structure used to generate the tips of the branches. A higher value results in better overhangs but the supports are harder to remove, thus it is recommended to enable top support interfaces instead of a high branch density value if dense interfaces are needed.

projections.label: Support wall loops
projections.tooltip: This setting specifies the count of support walls in the range of [0,2]. 0 means auto.

projections.label: Tree support with infill
projections.tooltip: This setting specifies whether to add infill inside large hollows of tree support.

projections.label: Use firmware retraction
projections.tooltip: This experimental setting uses G10 and G11 commands to have the firmware handle the retraction. This is only supported in recent Marlin.

projections.label: Use relative E distances
projections.tooltip: Relative extrusion is recommended when using "label_objects" option. Some extruders work better with this option unchecked (absolute extrusion mode). Wipe tower is only compatible with relative mode. It is recommended on most printers. Default is checked.

projections.label: Wall loop direction
projections.tooltip:
The direction which the wall loops are extruded when looking down from the top.

By default all walls are extruded in counter-clockwise, unless Reverse on even is enabled. Set this to any option other than Auto will force the wall direction regardless of the Reverse on even.

This option will be disabled if spiral vase mode is enabled.

projections.label: Wall distribution count
projections.tooltip: The number of walls, counted from the center, over which the variation needs to be spread. Lower values mean that the outer walls don't change in width.

projections.label: Walls
projections.tooltip: Filament to print walls.

projections.label: Wall generator
projections.tooltip: Classic wall generator produces walls with constant extrusion width and for very thin areas is used gap-fill. Arachne engine produces walls with variable extrusion width.

projections.label: Wall loops
projections.tooltip: Number of walls of every layer.

projections.label: Walls printing order
projections.tooltip:
Print sequence of the internal (inner) and external (outer) walls.

Use Inner/Outer for best overhangs. This is because the overhanging walls can adhere to a neighbouring perimeter while printing. However, this option results in slightly reduced surface quality as the external perimeter is deformed by being squashed to the internal perimeter.

Use Inner/Outer/Inner for the best external surface finish and dimensional accuracy as the external wall is printed undisturbed from an internal perimeter. However, overhang performance will reduce as there is no internal perimeter to print the external wall against. This option requires a minimum of 3 walls to be effective as it prints the internal walls from the 3rd perimeter onwards first, then the external perimeter and, finally, the first internal perimeter. This option is recommended against the Outer/Inner option in most cases.

Use Outer/Inner for the same external wall quality and dimensional accuracy benefits of Inner/Outer/Inner option. However, the z seams will appear less consistent as the first extrusion of a new layer starts on a visible surface.

projections.label: Wall transitioning threshold angle
projections.tooltip: When to create transitions between even and odd numbers of walls. A wedge shape with an angle greater than this setting will not have transitions and no walls will be printed in the center to fill the remaining space. Reducing this setting reduces the number and length of these center walls, but may leave gaps or overextrude.

projections.label: Wall transitioning filter margin
projections.tooltip: Prevent transitioning back and forth between one extra wall and one less. This margin extends the range of extrusion widths which follow to [Minimum wall width - margin, 2 * Minimum wall width + margin]. Increasing this margin reduces the number of transitions, which reduces the number of extrusion starts/stops and travel time. However, large extrusion width variation can lead to under- or overextrusion problems. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.

projections.label: Wall transition length
projections.tooltip: When transitioning between different numbers of walls as the part becomes thinner, a certain amount of space is allotted to split or join the wall segments. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.

projections.label: Wipe before external loop
projections.tooltip:
To minimize visibility of potential overextrusion at the start of an external perimeter when printing with Outer/Inner or Inner/Outer/Inner wall print order, the de-retraction is performed slightly on the inside from the start of the external perimeter. That way any potential over extrusion is hidden from the outside surface.

This is useful when printing with Outer/Inner or Inner/Outer/Inner wall print order as in these modes it is more likely an external perimeter is printed immediately after a de-retraction move.

projections.label: Wipe Distance
projections.tooltip:
Describe how long the nozzle will move along the last path when retracting.

Depending on how long the wipe operation lasts, how fast and long the extruder/filament retraction settings are, a retraction move may be needed to retract the remaining filament.

Setting a value in the retract amount before wipe setting below will perform any excess retraction before the wipe, else it will be performed after.

projections.label: Wipe on loops
projections.tooltip: To minimize the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, a small inward movement is executed before the extruder leaves the loop.

projections.label: Wipe speed
projections.tooltip: The wipe speed is determined by the speed setting specified in this configuration. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 80%), it will be calculated based on the travel speed setting above. The default value for this parameter is 80%.

projections.label: Maximal bridging distance
projections.tooltip: Maximal distance between supports on sparse infill sections.

projections.label: Stabilization cone apex angle
projections.tooltip: Angle at the apex of the cone that is used to stabilize the wipe tower. Larger angle means wider base.

projections.label: Extra flow for purging
projections.tooltip: Extra flow used for the purging lines on the wipe tower. This makes the purging lines thicker or narrower than they normally would be. The spacing is adjusted automatically.

projections.label: Extra rib length
projections.tooltip: Positive values can increase the size of the rib wall, while negative values can reduce the size. However, the size of the rib wall can not be smaller than that determined by the cleaning volume.

projections.label: Wipe tower purge lines spacing
projections.tooltip: Spacing of purge lines on the wipe tower.

projections.label: Wipe tower
projections.tooltip: The extruder to use when printing perimeter of the wipe tower. Set to 0 to use the one that is available (non-soluble would be preferred).

projections.label: Fillet wall
projections.tooltip: The wall of prime tower will fillet.

projections.label: Maximum wipe tower print speed
projections.tooltip:
The maximum print speed when purging in the wipe tower and printing the wipe tower sparse layers. When purging, if the sparse infill speed or calculated speed from the filament max volumetric speed is lower, the lowest will be used instead.

When printing the sparse layers, if the internal perimeter speed or calculated speed from the filament max volumetric speed is lower, the lowest will be used instead.

Increasing this speed may affect the tower's stability as well as increase the force with which the nozzle collides with any blobs that may have formed on the wipe tower.

Before increasing this parameter beyond the default of 90 mm/s, make sure your printer can reliably bridge at the increased speeds and that ooze when tool changing is well controlled.

For the wipe tower external perimeters the internal perimeter speed is used regardless of this setting.

projections.label: No sparse layers (beta)
projections.tooltip: If enabled, the wipe tower will not be printed on layers with no tool changes. On layers with a tool change, extruder will travel downward to print the wipe tower. User is responsible for ensuring there is no collision with the print.

projections.label: Rib width
projections.tooltip: Rib width.

projections.label: Wipe tower rotation angle
projections.tooltip: Wipe tower rotation angle with respect to X axis.

projections.label: Wall type
projections.tooltip:
Wipe tower outer wall type.
1. Rectangle: The default wall type, a rectangle with fixed width and height.
2. Cone: A cone with a fillet at the bottom to help stabilize the wipe tower.
3. Rib: Adds four ribs to the tower wall for enhanced stability.

projections.label: Wipe while retracting
projections.tooltip: Move nozzle along the last extrusion path when retracting to clean any leaked material on the nozzle. This can minimize blobs when printing a new part after traveling.

projections.label: Purging volumes - load/unload volumes
projections.tooltip: This vector saves required volumes to change from/to each tool used on the wipe tower. These values are used to simplify creation of the full purging volumes below.

projections.label: X-Y contour compensation
projections.tooltip: Contours of objects will expand or contract in the XY plane by the configured value. Positive values make contours bigger, negative values make contours smaller. This function is used to adjust sizes slightly when the objects have assembling issues.

projections.label: X-Y hole compensation
projections.tooltip: Holes in objects will expand or contract in the XY plane by the configured value. Positive values make holes bigger, negative values make holes smaller. This function is used to adjust sizes slightly when the objects have assembling issues.

projections.label: Z-hop type
projections.tooltip: Type of Z-hop.

projections.label: Z hop when moving to tower
Z-hop height
projections.tooltip: Whenever the retraction is done, the nozzle is lifted a little to create clearance between nozzle and the print. It prevents nozzle from hitting the print when travel move. Using spiral lines to lift Z can prevent stringing.

projections.label: Z offset
projections.tooltip: This value will be added (or subtracted) from all the Z coordinates in the output G-code. It is used to compensate for bad Z endstop position: for example, if your endstop zero actually leaves the nozzle 0.3mm far from the print bed, set this to -0.3 (or fix your endstop).

projections.label: Total volume
projections.tooltip: Total volume of filament used during the entire print.

projections.label: Volume per extruder
projections.tooltip: Total filament volume extruded per extruder during the entire print.

projections.label: Total weight
projections.tooltip: Total weight of the print. Calculated from filament_density value in Filament Settings.

projections.label: Weight per extruder
projections.tooltip: Weight per extruder extruded during the entire print. Calculated from filament_density value in Filament Settings.

projections.label: Total layer count
projections.tooltip: Number of layers in the entire print.

projections.label: Total tool changes
projections.tooltip: Number of tool changes during the print.

projections.label: Current Z-hop
projections.tooltip: Contains Z-hop present at the beginning of the custom G-code block.

projections.label: Absolute E position
projections.tooltip: Current position of the extruder axis. Only used with absolute extruder addressing.

projections.label: Extra de-retraction
projections.tooltip: Currently planned extra extruder priming after de-retraction.

projections.label: Retraction
projections.tooltip: Retraction state at the beginning of the custom G-code block. If the custom G-code moves the extruder axis, it should write to this variable so Snapmaker Orca de-retracts correctly when it gets control back.

projections.label: Position
projections.tooltip: Position of the extruder at the beginning of the custom G-code block. If the custom G-code travels somewhere else, it should write to this variable so Snapmaker Orca knows where it travels from when it gets control back.

projections.label: Initial layer bed temperature (initial extruder)
projections.tooltip: Initial layer bed temperature for the initial extruder. Same as bed_temperature_initial_layer[initial_extruder]

projections.label: Initial layer bed temperature
projections.tooltip: Vector of initial layer bed temperatures for each extruder/filament. Provides the same value as first_layer_bed_temperature.

projections.label: Bed temperature
projections.tooltip: Vector of bed temperatures for each extruder/filament.

projections.label: Chamber temperature
projections.tooltip: Vector of chamber temperatures for each extruder/filament.

projections.label: First layer bed temperature
projections.tooltip: Vector of first layer bed temperatures for each extruder/filament. Provides the same value as bed_temperature_initial_layer.

projections.label: First layer temperature
projections.tooltip: Vector of first layer temperatures for each extruder/filament.

projections.label: Overall chamber temperature
projections.tooltip: Overall chamber temperature. This value is the maximum chamber temperature of any extruder/filament used.

projections.label: Timestamp
projections.tooltip: String containing current time in yyyyMMdd-hhmmss format.

fields: Slicing height for each layer. Smaller layer height means more accurate and more printing time.
Height of initial layer. Making initial layer height to be thick slightly can improve build plate adhesion.
Line width of initial layer. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

Start height of the scarf.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current layer height. The default value for this parameter is 0.
Shrinks the initial layer on build plate to compensate for elephant foot effect.

The number of layers on which the elephant foot compensation will be active. The first layer will be shrunk by the elephant foot compensation value, then the next layers will be linearly shrunk less, up to the layer indicated by this value.
Improve shell precision by adjusting outer wall spacing. This also improves layer consistency. NOTE: This option will be ignored for outer-inner or inner-outer-inner wall sequences.

Enable this to get precise z height of object after slicing. It will get the precise object height by fine-tuning the layer heights of the last few layers. Note that this is an experimental parameter.

Search for almost-circular holes that span more than one layer and convert the geometry to polyholes. Use the nozzle size and the (biggest) diameter to compute the polyhole.
See http://hydraraptor.blogspot.com/2011/02/polyholes.html
Ironing is using small flow to print on same height of surface again to make flat surface more smooth. This setting controls which layer being ironed
The amount of material to extrude during ironing. Relative to flow of normal layer height. Too high value results in overextrusion on the surface.
The minimum wall width that should be used for the first layer is recommended to be set to the same size as the nozzle. This adjustment is expected to enhance adhesion.

Print sequence of the internal (inner) and external (outer) walls.

Use Inner/Outer for best overhangs. This is because the overhanging walls can adhere to a neighbouring perimeter while printing. However, this option results in slightly reduced surface quality as the external perimeter is deformed by being squashed to the internal perimeter.

Use Inner/Outer/Inner for the best external surface finish and dimensional accuracy as the external wall is printed undisturbed from an internal perimeter. However, overhang performance will reduce as there is no internal perimeter to print the external wall against. This option requires a minimum of 3 walls to be effective as it prints the internal walls from the 3rd perimeter onwards first, then the external perimeter and, finally, the first internal perimeter. This option is recommended against the Outer/Inner option in most cases.

Use Outer/Inner for the same external wall quality and dimensional accuracy benefits of Inner/Outer/Inner option. However, the z seams will appear less consistent as the first extrusion of a new layer starts on a visible surface.

If a top surface has to be printed and it's partially covered by another layer, it won't be considered at a top layer where its width is below this value. This can be useful to not let the 'one perimeter on top' trigger on surface that should be covered only by perimeters. This value can be a mm or a % of the perimeter extrusion width.
Warning: If enabled, artifacts can be created if you have some thin features on the next layer, like letters. Set this setting to 0 to remove these artifacts.
Only one wall on first layer
Use only one wall on first layer, to give more space to the bottom infill pattern.

This value governs the thickness of the internal bridge layer. This is the first layer over sparse infill. Decrease this value slightly (for example 0.9) to improve surface quality over sparse infill.

The actual internal bridge flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the bridge flow ratio, the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

This option enables the generation of an extra bridge layer over internal and/or external bridges.

Extra bridge layers help improve bridge appearance and reliability, as the solid infill is better supported. This is especially useful in fast printers, where the bridge and solid infill speeds vary greatly. The extra bridge layer results in reduced pillowing on top surfaces, as well as reduced separation of the external bridge layer from its surrounding perimeters.

It is generally recommended to set this to at least 'External bridge only', unless specific issues with the sliced model are found.

Options:
1. Disabled - does not generate second bridge layers. This is the default and is set for compatibility purposes
2. External bridge only - generates second bridge layers for external-facing bridges only. Please note that small bridges that are shorter or narrower than the set number of perimeters will be skipped as they would not benefit from a second bridge layer. If generated, the second bridge layer will be extruded parallel to the first bridge layer to reinforce the bridge strength
3. Internal bridge only - generates second bridge layers for internal bridges over sparse infill only. Please note that the internal bridges count towards the top shell layer count of your model. The second internal bridge layer will be extruded as close to perpendicular to the first as possible. If multiple regions in the same island, with varying bridge angles are present, the last region of that island will be selected as the angle reference
4. Apply to all - generates second bridge layers for both internal and external-facing bridges

This option can help reduce pillowing on top surfaces in heavily slanted or curved models.
By default, small internal bridges are filtered out and the internal solid infill is printed directly over the sparse infill. This works well in most cases, speeding up printing without too much compromise on top surface quality.
However, in heavily slanted or curved models, especially where too low a sparse infill density is used, this may result in curling of the unsupported solid infill, causing pillowing.
Enabling limited filtering or no filtering will print internal bridge layer over slightly unsupported internal solid infill. The options below control the sensitivity of the filtering, i.e. they control where internal bridges are created:
1. Filter - enables this option. This is the default behavior and works well in most cases
2. Limited filtering - creates internal bridges on heavily slanted surfaces while avoiding unnecessary bridges. This works well for most difficult models
3. No filtering - creates internal bridges on every potential internal overhang. This option is useful for heavily slanted top surface models; however, in most cases, it creates too many unnecessary bridges

This option creates bridges for counterbore holes, allowing them to be printed without support. Available modes include:
1. None: No bridge is created
2. Partially Bridged: Only a part of the unsupported area will be bridged
3. Sacrificial Layer: A full sacrificial bridge layer is created

Extrude perimeters that have a part over an overhang in the reverse direction on even layers. This alternating pattern can drastically improve steep overhangs.

This setting can also help reduce part warping due to the reduction of stresses in the part walls.

Apply the reverse perimeters logic only on internal perimeters.

This setting greatly reduces part stresses as they are now distributed in alternating directions. This should reduce part warping while also maintaining external wall quality. This feature can be very useful for warp prone material, like ABS/ASA, and also for elastic filaments, like TPU and Silk PLA. It can also help reduce warping on floating regions over supports.

For this setting to be the most effective, it is recommended to set the Reverse Threshold to 0 so that all internal walls print in alternating directions on even layers irrespective of their overhang degree.

Number of mm the overhang need to be for the reversal to be considered useful. Can be a % of the perimeter width.
Value 0 enables reversal on every even layers regardless.
When Detect overhang wall is not enabled, this option is ignored and reversal happens on every even layers regardless.
Number of walls of every layer.

This setting adds an extra wall to every other layer. This way the infill gets wedged vertically between the walls, resulting in stronger prints.

When this option is enabled, the ensure vertical shell thickness option needs to be disabled.

Using lightning infill together with this option is not recommended as there is limited infill to anchor the extra perimeters to.

This is the number of solid layers of top shell, including the top surface layer. When the thickness calculated by this value is thinner than top shell thickness, the top shell layers will be increased.

The number of top solid layers is increased when slicing if the thickness calculated by top shell layers is thinner than this value. This can avoid having too thin shell when layer height is small. 0 means that this setting is disabled and thickness of top shell is absolutely determined by top shell layers.

This is the number of solid layers of bottom shell, including the bottom surface layer. When the thickness calculated by this value is thinner than bottom shell thickness, the bottom shell layers will be increased.

The number of bottom solid layers is increased when slicing if the thickness calculated by bottom shell layers is thinner than this value. This can avoid having too thin shell when layer height is small. 0 means that this setting is disabled and thickness of bottom shell is absolutely determined by bottom shell layers.

Rotate the sparse infill direction per layer using a template of angles. Enter comma-separated degrees (e.g., '0,30,60,90'). Angles are applied in order by layer and repeat when the list ends. Advanced syntax is supported: '+5' rotates +5° every layer; '+5#5' rotates +5° every 5 layers. See the Wiki for details. When a template is set, the standard infill direction setting is ignored. Note: some infill patterns (e.g., Gyroid) control rotation themselves; use with care.
This parameter adds a slight displacement to each layer of infill to create a cross texture.

This parameter adds a rotation of solid infill direction to each layer according to the specified template. The template is a comma-separated list of angles in degrees, e.g. '0,90'. The first angle is applied to the first layer, the second angle to the second layer, and so on. If there are more layers than angles, the angles will be repeated. Note that not all solid infill patterns support rotation.

Insert solid infill at specific layers. Use N to insert every Nth layer, N#K to insert K consecutive solid layers every N layers (K is optional, e.g. '5#' equals '5#1'), or a comma-separated list (e.g. 1,7,9) to insert at explicit layers. Layers are 1-based.
Automatically Combine sparse infill of several layers to print together to reduce time. Wall is still printed with original layer height.

Maximum layer height for the combined sparse infill.

Set it to 0 or 100% to use the nozzle diameter (for maximum reduction in print time) or a value of ~80% to maximize sparse infill strength.

The number of layers over which infill is combined is derived by dividing this value with the layer height and rounded down to the nearest decimal.

Use either absolute mm values (eg. 0.32mm for a 0.4mm nozzle) or % values (eg 80%). This value must not be larger than the nozzle diameter.

Add solid infill near sloping surfaces to guarantee the vertical shell thickness (top+bottom solid layers)
None: No solid infill will be added anywhere. Caution: Use this option carefully if your model has sloped surfaces
Critical Only: Avoid adding solid infill for walls
Moderate: Add solid infill for heavily sloping surfaces only
All: Add solid infill for all suitable sloping surfaces
Default value is All.
Speed of initial layer except the solid infill part.
Speed of solid infill part of initial layer.
The first few layers are printed slower than normal. The speed is gradually increased in a linear fashion over the specified number of layers.

Enable this option to slow down printing in areas where perimeters may have curled upwards. For example, additional slowdown will be applied when printing overhangs on sharp corners like the front of the Benchy hull, reducing curling which compounds over multiple layers.

It is generally recommended to have this option switched on unless your printer cooling is powerful enough or the print speed slow enough that perimeter curling does not happen. If printing with a high external perimeter speed, this parameter may introduce slight artifacts when slowing down due to the large variance in print speeds. If you notice artifacts, ensure your pressure advance is tuned correctly.

Note: When this option is enabled, overhang perimeters are treated like overhangs, meaning the overhang speed is applied even if the overhanging perimeter is part of a bridge. For example, when the perimeters are 100% overhanging, with no wall supporting them from underneath, the 100% overhang speed will be applied.
The default acceleration of both normal printing and travel except initial layer.
Acceleration of initial layer. Using a lower value can improve build plate adhesion.
Density of the first raft or support layer.
Expand the first raft or support layer to improve bed plate adhesion.
Object will be raised by this number of support layers. Use this function to avoid warping when printing ABS.
The amount of material to extrude during ironing. Relative to flow of normal support interface layer height. Too high value results in overextrusion on the surface.
XY separation between an object and its support at the first layer.
Support layer uses layer height independent with object layer. This is to support customizing z-gap and save print time. This option will be invalid when the prime tower is enabled.
Enabling this option means the height of tree support layer except the first will be automatically calculated.
Enable gradual layer-by-layer reduction of the brim around the prime tower. This creates a chamfered/tapered effect, reducing material usage while maintaining first layer adhesion.
Maximum width of the chamfer zone measured from the tower perimeter. The brim will reduce within this distance. Larger values create a more gradual taper but take more layers to complete.

The maximum print speed when purging in the wipe tower and printing the wipe tower sparse layers. When purging, if the sparse infill speed or calculated speed from the filament max volumetric speed is lower, the lowest will be used instead.

When printing the sparse layers, if the internal perimeter speed or calculated speed from the filament max volumetric speed is lower, the lowest will be used instead.

Increasing this speed may affect the tower's stability as well as increase the force with which the nozzle collides with any blobs that may have formed on the wipe tower.

Before increasing this parameter beyond the default of 90 mm/s, make sure your printer can reliably bridge at the increased speeds and that ooze when tool changing is well controlled.

For the wipe tower external perimeters the internal perimeter speed is used regardless of this setting.

If enabled, the wipe tower will not be printed on layers with no tool changes. On layers with a tool change, extruder will travel downward to print the wipe tower. User is responsible for ensuring there is no collision with the print.
The height of the beams of the interlocking structure, measured in number of layers. Less layers is stronger, but more prone to defects.
Enable "Subdivide Mix Layer" for mixing areas. Layer height will be subdivided for better color mixing results.

Experimental. Apply Local-Z thinning across whole mixed-color regions instead of limiting the effect strictly to painted mixed masks.

Only available when Subdivide Mix Layer is enabled.

Experimental. When Subdivide Mix Layer is enabled, also apply the same subdivision to infill inside mixed-color areas.

This is enabled automatically with Subdivide Mix Layer. Turn it off to keep infill on the normal layer height.

It can improve internal color mixing, but may add toolchanges and affect infill behavior.
Speed of skirt, in mm/s. Zero means use default layer extrusion speed.
How many layers of skirt. Usually only one layer.
Limits the skirt/draft shield loops to one wall after the first layer. This is useful, on occasion, to conserve filament but may cause the draft shield/skirt to warp / crack.
Print sequence, layer by layer or object by object.
Print order within a single layer.
Spiralize smooths out the z moves of the outer contour. And turns a solid model into a single walled print with solid bottom layers. The final generated model has no seam.

Sets the starting flow ratio while transitioning from the last bottom layer to the spiral. Normally the spiral transition scales the flow ratio from 0% to 100% during the first loop which can in some cases lead to under extrusion at the start of the spiral.

If smooth or traditional mode is selected, a timelapse video will be generated for each print. After each layer is printed, a snapshot is taken with the chamber camera. All of these snapshots are composed into a timelapse video when printing completes. If smooth mode is selected, the toolhead will move to the excess chute after each layer is printed and then take a snapshot. Since the melt filament may leak from the nozzle during the process of taking a snapshot, prime tower is required for smooth mode to wipe nozzle.

Fuzzy skin generation mode. Works only with Arachne!
Displacement: Сlassic mode when the pattern is formed by shifting the nozzle sideways from the original path.
Extrusion: The mode when the pattern formed by the amount of extruded plastic. This is the fast and straight algorithm without unnecessary nozzle shake that gives a smooth pattern. But it is more useful for forming loose walls in the entire they array.
Combined: Joint mode [Displacement] + [Extrusion]. The appearance of the walls is similar to [Displacement] Mode, but it leaves no pores between the perimeters.

Attention! The [Extrusion] and [Combined] modes works only the fuzzy_skin_thickness parameter not more than the thickness of printed loop. At the same time, the width of the extrusion for a particular layer should also not be below a certain level. It is usually equal 15-25%% of a layer height. Therefore, the maximum fuzzy skin thickness with a perimeter width of 0.4 mm and a layer height of 0.2 mm will be 0.4-(0.2*0.25)=±0.35mm! If you enter a higher parameter than this, the error Flow::spacing() will displayed, and the model will not be sliced. You can choose this number until this error is repeated.
Apply fuzzy skin to first layer
Whether to apply fuzzy skin on the first layer.

For high-temperature materials like ABS, ASA, PC, and PA, a higher chamber temperature can help suppress or reduce warping and potentially lead to higher interlayer bonding strength. However, at the same time, a higher chamber temperature will reduce the efficiency of air filtration for ABS and ASA.

For PLA, PETG, TPU, PVA, and other low-temperature materials, this option should be disabled (set to 0) as the chamber temperature should be low to avoid extruder clogging caused by material softening at the heat break.

If enabled, this parameter also sets a G-code variable named chamber_temperature, which can be used to pass the desired chamber temperature to your print start macro, or a heat soak macro like this: PRINT_START (other variables) CHAMBER_TEMP=[chamber_temperature]. This may be useful if your printer does not support M141/M191 commands, or if you desire to handle heat soaking in the print start macro if no active chamber heater is installed.
Turn off all cooling fans for the first few layers. This can be used to improve build plate adhesion.

Fan speed will be ramped up linearly from zero at layer "close_fan_the_first_x_layers" to maximum at layer "full_fan_speed_layer". "full_fan_speed_layer" will be ignored if lower than "close_fan_the_first_x_layers", in which case the fan will be running at maximum allowed speed at layer "close_fan_the_first_x_layers" + 1.
Slow printing down for better layer cooling

Enable this option to slow printing speed down to make the final layer time not shorter than the layer time threshold in "Max fan speed threshold", so that layer can be cooled for longer time. This can improve the cooling quality for needle and small details.

If enabled, this setting will ensure external perimeters are not slowed down to meet the minimum layer time. This is particularly helpful in the below scenarios:
1. To avoid changes in shine when printing glossy filaments
2. To avoid changes in external wall speed which may create slight wall artifacts that appear like Z banding
3. To avoid printing at speeds which cause VFAs (fine artifacts) on the external walls
The minimum print speed to which the printer slows down to maintain the minimum layer time defined above when the slowdown for better layer cooling is enabled.

When the overhang exceeds this specified threshold, force the cooling fan to run at the 'Overhang Fan Speed' set below. This threshold is expressed as a percentage, indicating the portion of each line's width that is unsupported by the layer beneath it. Setting this value to 0% forces the cooling fan to run for all outer walls, regardless of the overhang degree.

Use this part cooling fan speed when printing bridges or overhang walls with an overhang threshold that exceeds the value set in the 'Overhangs cooling threshold' parameter above. Increasing the cooling specifically for overhangs and bridges can improve the overall print quality of these features.

Please note, this fan speed is clamped on the lower end by the minimum fan speed threshold set above. It is also adjusted upwards up to the maximum fan speed threshold when the minimum layer time threshold is not met.

This part cooling fan speed is applied when printing support interfaces. Setting this parameter to a higher than regular speed reduces the layer binding strength between supports and the supported part, making them easier to separate.
Set to -1 to disable it.
This setting is overridden by disable_fan_first_layers.

Speed of auxiliary part cooling fan. Auxiliary fan will run at this speed during printing except the first several layers which is defined by no cooling layers.
Please enable auxiliary_fan in printer settings to use this feature. G-code command: M106 P2 S(0-255)
The lowest printable layer height for the extruder. Used to limit the minimum layer height when enable adaptive layer height.
The highest printable layer height for the extruder. Used to limit the maximum layer height when enable adaptive layer height.
Force a retraction when changes layer.

Distribute mixed filament layer-cycle cadence using an advanced ordered dithering pattern instead of a simple contiguous A-then-B run. This can reduce visible striping for some hues.

This is an even more experimental mode and the perceived color may differ from normal dithering for the same filament pair and ratio.

Detailed mixed filament setting explanations will be published once the project wiki is available.

Merge ordinary mixed-filament painted regions into a single area when they resolve to the same physical filament on a layer.

This improves continuity for adjacent same-color areas.

Subdivide Mix Layer disables this behavior, and gradient mixed regions also bypass it because they use the Local-Z pipeline.

Layer height contribution of component A for dithering virtual filaments. Set to 0 to use normal 1-layer A / 1-layer B alternation.

Detailed mixed filament setting explanations will be published once the project wiki is available.

Layer height contribution of component B for dithering virtual filaments. Set to 0 to use normal 1-layer A / 1-layer B alternation.

Detailed mixed filament setting explanations will be published once the project wiki is available.

Layer height used in Z zones painted with dithering (mixed virtual filaments). Set to 0 to keep normal layer height in those zones.

Detailed mixed filament setting explanations will be published once the project wiki is available.

Show and apply the per-row mixed filament Bias control.

When enabled, the selected filament in a mixed pair is recessed slightly so the other component becomes more visible.

Bias is ignored for grouped wall patterns, same-layer pointillisme, and Local Z dithering.

Enable height-weighted cadence for mixed filaments. Limitation: only one height-weighted mixed color should be present at a given Z plane, because independent per-color layer heights are not supported and the resulting layer height applies to the whole plane. When disabled, layer-cycle cadence is used.

Detailed mixed filament setting explanations will be published once the project wiki is available.

Lower bound used when Local-Z mixed-filament dithering chooses per-color sublayer heights.

Smaller values let Local-Z use thinner sublayers for a color when needed.

Detailed mixed filament setting explanations will be published once the project wiki is available.

Upper bound used when Local-Z mixed-filament dithering chooses per-color sublayer heights.

Larger values let Local-Z use thicker sublayers for a color when needed.

Detailed mixed filament setting explanations will be published once the project wiki is available.

Optional non-extruded spacing between adjacent pointillisme segments. Increase carefully to improve separation and print quality.

Warning: Same-layer pointillisme is extremely experimental and may produce unusable results.

Length of one pointillisme segment along an extrusion path for same-layer pointillisme mode. Set to 0 to use automatic nozzle-based sizing.

Warning: Same-layer pointillisme is extremely experimental and may produce unusable results.

XY offset applied to mixed-filament painted regions before region assignment.

Positive values contract the mixed zone inward. Negative values expand it outward.

This applies to mixed filament usage in layer cadence, height cadence, same-layer pointillisme, and local Z dithering.

Experimental. For mixed rows with 3 or more physical filaments, allocate Local-Z sublayers directly across all components with carry-over error between layers instead of collapsing them into pair cadence.

This can reduce visible banding in multicolor Local-Z blends at the cost of more toolchanges. It is ignored when explicit Local-Z A/B heights are set.

When enabled, dithering Z step size is applied only where mixed filament is painted. Unpainted zones keep their original layer height.

Detailed mixed filament setting explanations will be published once the project wiki is available.

Density of the bottom surface layer. Intended for aesthetic or functional purposes, not to fix issues such as over-extrusion.
WARNING: Lowering this value may negatively affect bed adhesion.

Density of top surface layer. A value of 100% creates a fully solid, smooth top layer. Reducing this value results in a textured top surface, according to the chosen top surface pattern. A value of 0% will result in only the walls on the top layer being created. Intended for aesthetic or functional purposes, not to fix issues such as over-extrusion.
Cover the top contact layer of the supports with loops. Disabled by default.
Expand all raft layers in XY plane.
This G-code is inserted at every layer change before the Z lift.
Bed temperature of the initial layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Cool Plate.
Bed temperature of the initial layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Engineering Plate.
Bed temperature of the initial layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Graphic Effect Plate.

Nozzle temperature for printing initial layer when using this filament.

Bed temperature for layers except the initial one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Cool Plate.

Bed temperature for layers except the initial one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Textured Cool Plate.
Bed temperature for layers except the initial one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Textured PEI Plate.
